  "new_string": "# ============================================================================\n# Benchmark Endpoints (Updated 2025-12-30 - Connected to BenchmarkKnowledgeDB)\n# ============================================================================\n\n# Pydantic models for benchmark API\nclass BenchmarkQueryRequest(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Request model for benchmark queries.\"\"\"\n    query: str = Field(..., description=\"Natural language query about tool performance\")\n    constraints: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict, description=\"Context constraints\")\n    top_k: int = Field(default=5, description=\"Number of results to return\")\n\n\nclass ToolComparisonRequest(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Request model for tool comparison.\"\"\"\n    tool_a: str = Field(..., description=\"First tool name\")\n    tool_b: str = Field(..., description=\"Second tool name\")\n    task: Optional[str] = Field(None, description=\"Task context for comparison\")\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \"/api/ai_assistant/benchmarks/{scenario}\",\n    summary=\"Get benchmark results for a scenario.\"\n)\ndef get_benchmark_results(\n    scenario: str = Path(..., description=\"Benchmark scenario name\"),\n    trans: ProvidesUserContext = DependsOnTrans\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Get benchmark comparison results for tools/parameters.\n\n    Available scenarios:\n    - rna_seq_alignment: RNA-seq read alignment tool comparison\n    - variant_calling: Variant calling tool comparison\n    - single_cell_integration: Single-cell batch integration comparison\n    - differential_expression: Differential expression analysis comparison\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        # Try to use BenchmarkKnowledgeDB first (primary source)\n        if BENCHMARK_AVAILABLE and BenchmarkKnowledgeDB:\n            try:\n                benchmark_db = BenchmarkKnowledgeDB()\n\n                # Query the benchmark database with the scenario as search term\n                results = benchmark_db.query_semantic(scenario, top_k=10)\n\n                if results:\n                    tools_compared = []\n                    metrics = {}\n                    recommendations = []\n\n                    for result in results:\n                        tool_name = result.get('tool_name', '')\n                        if tool_name and tool_name not in tools_compared:\n                            tools_compared.append(tool_name)\n\n                        # Collect metrics\n                        if result.get('metric_name') and result.get('metric_value'):\n                            key = f\"{tool_name}_{result['metric_name']}\"\n                            metrics[key] = {\n                                'tool': tool_name,\n                                'metric': result['metric_name'],\n                                'value': result['metric_value'],\n                                'rank': result.get('rank')\n                            }\n\n                        # Get recommendations from decision rules\n                        if result.get('evidence_text'):\n                            recommendations.append({\n                                'tool': tool_name,\n                                'evidence': result['evidence_text'],\n                                'doi': result.get('doi')\n                            })\n\n                    return {\n                        \"scenario\": scenario,\n                        \"available\": True,\n                        \"tools_compared\": tools_compared,\n                        \"metrics\": metrics,\n                        \"recommendations\": recommendations[:5],\n                        \"source\": \"benchmark_knowledge_db\"\n                    }\n            except Exception as db_err:\n                log.warning(f\"BenchmarkKnowledgeDB query failed: {db_err}\")\n\n        # Fallback to test harness\n        try:\n            from galaxy.ai.test_harness import load_benchmark_results\n            results = load_benchmark_results(scenario)\n            if results:\n                return {\n                    \"scenario\": scenario,\n                    \"available\": True,\n                    \"tools_compared\": results.get(\"tools\", []),\n                    \"metrics\": results.get(\"metrics\", {}),\n                    \"recommendations\": results.get(\"recommendations\", []),\n                    \"last_run\": results.get(\"timestamp\"),\n                    \"source\": \"test_harness\"\n                }\n        except ImportError:\n            pass\n\n        # No data available\n        return {\n            \"scenario\": scenario,\n            \"available\": False,\n            \"message\": \"No benchmark data available for this scenario\",\n            \"tools_compared\": [],\n            \"metrics\": {},\n            \"recommendations\": []\n        }\n\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.error(f\"Error fetching benchmarks: {e}\")\n        return {\n            \"scenario\": scenario,\n            \"available\": False,\n            \"error\": str(e)\n        }\n\n\n@router.post(\n    \"/api/ai_assistant/benchmark_query\",\n    summary=\"Query benchmarks with natural language.\"\n)\ndef query_benchmarks(\n    request: BenchmarkQueryRequest,\n    trans: ProvidesUserContext = DependsOnTrans\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Query benchmark knowledge with natural language.\n\n    Example queries:\n    - \"best RNA-seq aligner\"\n    - \"fastest variant caller for WGS\"\n    - \"memory-efficient single-cell integration\"\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if not BENCHMARK_AVAILABLE or not BenchmarkKnowledgeDB:\n            return {\n                \"success\": False,\n                \"error\": \"Benchmark knowledge system not available\"\n            }\n\n        benchmark_db = BenchmarkKnowledgeDB()\n\n        # Use semantic query\n        results = benchmark_db.query_semantic(request.query, top_k=request.top_k)\n\n        if not results:\n            return {\n                \"success\": True,\n                \"query\": request.query,\n                \"results\": [],\n                \"message\": \"No matching benchmarks found\"\n            }\n\n        # Get the best tool\n        best_result = results[0] if results else None\n        best_tool = best_result.get('tool_name') if best_result else None\n\n        # Format results\n        formatted_results = []\n        for result in results:\n            formatted_results.append({\n                \"tool\": result.get('tool_name'),\n                \"rank\": result.get('rank'),\n                \"metric\": result.get('metric_name'),\n                \"value\": result.get('metric_value'),\n                \"evidence\": result.get('evidence_text'),\n                \"study\": result.get('study_name'),\n                \"doi\": result.get('doi')\n            })\n\n        # Check for context-aware recommendations\n        recommendation = None\n        if request.constraints:\n            rec = benchmark_db.get_recommendation_for_condition(\n                condition_type=list(request.constraints.keys())[0] if request.constraints else None,\n                condition_value=list(request.constraints.values())[0] if request.constraints else None\n            )\n            if rec:\n                recommendation = {\n                    \"tool\": rec.get('tool_name'),\n                    \"reason\": rec.get('recommendation_text'),\n                    \"condition\": request.constraints\n                }\n\n        return {\n            \"success\": True,\n            \"query\": request.query,\n            \"best_tool\": best_tool,\n            \"evidence\": best_result.get('evidence_text') if best_result else None,\n            \"results\": formatted_results,\n            \"recommendation\": recommendation\n        }\n\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.error(f\"Error querying benchmarks: {e}\")\n        return {\n            \"success\": False,\n            \"error\": str(e)\n        }\n\n\n@router.post(\n    \"/api/ai_assistant/tool_comparison\",\n    summary=\"Compare two tools with benchmark evidence.\"\n)\ndef compare_tools(\n    request: ToolComparisonRequest,\n    trans: ProvidesUserContext = DependsOnTrans\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Compare two tools using benchmark evidence.\n\n    Returns winner, detailed comparison, and supporting evidence.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        if not BENCHMARK_AVAILABLE or not BenchmarkKnowledgeDB:\n            return {\n                \"success\": False,\n                \"error\": \"Benchmark knowledge system not available\"\n            }\n\n        benchmark_db = BenchmarkKnowledgeDB()\n\n        # Use the compare_tools method from BenchmarkKnowledgeDB\n        comparison = benchmark_db.compare_tools(request.tool_a, request.tool_b, request.task)\n\n        if not comparison:\n            return {\n                \"success\": True,\n                \"tool_a\": request.tool_a,\n                \"tool_b\": request.tool_b,\n                \"comparison_available\": False,\n                \"message\": f\"No benchmark data available comparing {request.tool_a} and {request.tool_b}\"\n            }\n\n        return {\n            \"success\": True,\n            \"tool_a\": request.tool_a,\n            \"tool_b\": request.tool_b,\n            \"comparison_available\": True,\n            \"winner\": comparison.get('winner'),\n            \"comparison\": comparison.get('comparison', {}),\n            \"evidence_text\": comparison.get('evidence_text'),\n            \"studies\": comparison.get('studies', []),\n            \"recommendation\": comparison.get('recommendation')\n        }\n\n    except Exception as e:\n        log.error(f\"Error comparing tools: {e}\")\n        return {\n            \"success\": False,\n            \"error\": str(e)\n        }"
}

=========================================================================\n    # UNIFIED INTENT ROUTING API (Added 2025-12-30)\n    # =========================================================================\n\n    def classify_intent(\n        self,\n        query: str,\n        context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None\n    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Classify the intent of a user query.\n\n        Routes to appropriate handler:\n        - workflow_generation \u2192 AgentOrchestrator\n        - research_question \u2192 ResearchAgent\n        - result_comparison \u2192 ResearchAgent + BenchmarkKnowledge\n        - tool_search \u2192 UnifiedToolSearch\n        - benchmark_query \u2192 BenchmarkKnowledgeDB (direct)\n\n        Args:\n            query: User's query text\n            context: Optional context (previous messages, domain, etc.)\n\n        Returns:\n            Dict with:\n            - intent: Primary intent type\n            - confidence: Classification confidence\n            - handler: Recommended handler\n            - requires_workflow: Whether workflow generation is needed\n            - requires_literature: Whether literature search is needed\n            - requires_benchmark: Whether benchmark data is needed\n            - entities: Extracted entities (tools, analysis types, etc.)\n        \"\"\"\n        if not INTENT_ROUTER_AVAILABLE or not self.intent_router:\n            # Fallback to simple keyword detection\n            return self._simple_intent_classify(query)\n\n        classification = self.intent_router.classify(query, context)\n\n        return {\n            \"intent\": classification.primary_intent.value,\n            \"confidence\": classification.confidence,\n            \"handler\": self.intent_router.get_handler_for_intent(classification.primary_intent),\n            \"secondary_intents\": [i.value for i in classification.secondary_intents],\n            \"requires_workflow\": classification.requires_workflow,\n            \"requires_literature\": classification.requires_literature,\n            \"requires_benchmark\": classification.requires_benchmark,\n            \"entities\": classification.extracted_entities,\n            \"routing_method\": classification.routing_method\n        }\n\n    def _simple_intent_classify(self, query: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Simple keyword-based intent classification as fallback.\"\"\"\n        query_lower = query.lower()\n\n        # Simple rules\n        if any(w in query_lower for w in ['workflow', 'pipeline', 'run analysis', 'process']):\n            intent = 'workflow_generation'\n            handler = 'agent_orchestrator'\n        elif any(w in query_lower for w in ['compare', 'vs', 'better', 'best']):\n            intent = 'result_comparison'\n            handler = 'research_agent'\n        elif any(w in query_lower for w in ['benchmark', 'performance']):\n            intent = 'benchmark_query'\n            handler = 'benchmark_knowledge'\n        elif any(w in query_lower for w in ['find tool', 'search tool', 'available tools']):\n            intent = 'tool_search'\n            handler = 'unified_tool_search'\n        else:\n            intent = 'research_question'\n            handler = 'research_agent'\n\n        return {\n            \"intent\": intent,\n            \"confidence\": 0.6,\n            \"handler\": handler,\n            \"secondary_intents\": [],\n            \"requires_workflow\": intent == 'workflow_generation',\n            \"requires_literature\": intent in ['research_question', 'result_comparison'],\n            \"requires_benchmark\": intent in ['result_comparison', 'benchmark_query'],\n            \"entities\": {},\n            \"routing_method\": \"simple_fallback\"\n        }\n\n    async def route_and_handle(\n        self,\n        query: str,\n        context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None\n    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Route a query to the appropriate handler and execute.\n\n        This is the main entry point for the unified AI assistant that\n        automatically determines intent and routes to the right component.\n\n        Args:\n            query: User's query text\n            context: Optional context\n\n        Returns:\n            Response from the appropriate handler\n        \"\"\"\n        # Step 1: Classify intent\n        classification = self.classify_intent(query, context)\n\n        # Step 2: Route to handler\n        handler = classification.get('handler', 'research_agent')\n        intent = classification.get('intent', 'research_question')\n\n        try:\n            if handler == 'agent_orchestrator':\n                # Workflow generation\n                return await self._handle_workflow_generation(query, context)\n\n            elif handler == 'research_agent':\n                # Research questions, comparisons, conclusions\n                return await self._handle_research_query(query, classification, context)\n\n            elif handler == 'benchmark_knowledge':\n                # Direct benchmark queries\n                return self._handle_benchmark_query(query)\n\n            elif handler == 'unified_tool_search':\n                # Tool search\n                return self._handle_tool_search(query, context)\n\n            else:\n                # Default to research agent\n                return await self._handle_research_query(query, classification, context)\n\n        except Exception as e:\n            log.error(f\"Error handling query: {e}\")\n            return {\n                \"success\": False,\n                \"error\": str(e),\n                \"intent\": intent,\n                \"handler\": handler\n            }\n\n    async def _handle_workflow_generation(\n        self,\n        query: str,\n        context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None\n    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Handle workflow generation requests.\"\"\"\n        # Use the existing generate_workflow_unified method\n        datasets = context.get('datasets', []) if context else []\n        result = self.generate_workflow_unified(query, available_datasets=datasets)\n        return {\n            \"success\": result.get('success', False),\n            \"handler\": \"agent_orchestrator\",\n            \"workflow\": result.get('workflow_ga'),\n            \"source\": result.get('source'),\n            \"confidence\": result.get('confidence'),\n            \"message\": result.get('message')\n        }\n\n    async def _handle_research_query(\n        self,\n        query: str,\n        classification: Dict[str, Any],\n        context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None\n    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Handle research questions using ResearchAgent.\"\"\"\n        if not self.research_agent:\n            # Fallback to benchmark query\n            return self._handle_benchmark_query(query)\n\n        response = self.research_agent.answer_question_sync(\n            question=query,\n            context=context,\n            include_citations=True,\n            include_benchmark_evidence=classification.get('requires_benchmark', True)\n        )\n\n        return {\n            \"success\": not response.error,\n            \"handler\": \"research_agent\",\n            \"answer\": response.answer,\n            \"citations\": [\n                {\"title\": c.title, \"doi\": c.doi, \"year\": c.year}\n                for c in response.citations\n            ],\n            \"benchmark_evidence\": response.benchmark_evidence,\n            \"confidence\": response.confidence,\n            \"follow_up_questions\": response.follow_up_questions\n        }\n\n    def _handle_benchmark_query(self, query: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Handle direct benchmark queries.\"\"\"\n        result = self.query_benchmark(query, top_k=5)\n        return {\n            \"success\": True,\n            \"handler\": \"benchmark_knowledge\",\n            \"best_tool\": result.get('best_tool'),\n            \"evidence\": result.get('evidence'),\n            \"results\": result.get('results', [])\n        }\n\n    def _handle_tool_search(\n        self,\n        query: str,\n        context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None\n    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Handle tool search requests.\"\"\"\n        # Use existing tool search\n        tools = self.workflow_search.search_tools(query, limit=10)\n        return {\n            \"success\": True,\n            \"handler\": \"unified_tool_search\",\n            \"tools\": tools,\n            \"count\": len(tools)\n        }\n\n    # =========================================================================\n    # BENCHMARK KNOWLEDGE API (For ResearchAgent and Workflow Generation)\n    # ========================================================================="
}

studies with DOI links.\n * Integrates with the ResearchAgent for literature-backed tool comparisons.\n */\n\nimport { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from \"@/components/ui/card\";\nimport { Badge } from \"@/components/ui/badge\";\nimport { Button } from \"@/components/ui/button\";\nimport { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger, TooltipProvider } from \"@/components/ui/tooltip\";\nimport {\n  BarChart3,\n  Trophy,\n  ExternalLink,\n  ChevronRight,\n  ChevronDown,\n  BookOpen,\n  Beaker,\n  Info,\n  Award,\n  TrendingUp,\n  Clock,\n  Zap,\n} from \"lucide-react\";\nimport { cn } from \"@/lib/utils\";\nimport { useState } from \"react\";\n\n// Types for benchmark evidence data\nexport interface BenchmarkToolResult {\n  tool_name: string;\n  galaxy_tool_id?: string;\n  rank: number;\n  metric_name: string;\n  metric_value: number | string;\n  metric_unit?: string;\n  evidence_text?: string;\n  context_notes?: string;\n}\n\nexport interface BenchmarkStudy {\n  study_name: string;\n  doi?: string;\n  pmid?: string;\n  year?: number;\n  dataset_name?: string;\n  dataset_type?: string;\n}\n\nexport interface BenchmarkComparison {\n  query?: string;\n  task?: string;\n  best_tool?: string;\n  winner?: string;\n  evidence?: string;\n  recommendation?: string;\n  results: BenchmarkToolResult[];\n  study?: BenchmarkStudy;\n  comparison?: Record<string, Record<string, number | string>>;\n}\n\ninterface BenchmarkEvidenceProps {\n  benchmarkData: BenchmarkComparison;\n  onToolClick?: (toolName: string, galaxyToolId?: string) => void;\n  className?: string;\n}\n\nexport function BenchmarkEvidence({\n  benchmarkData,\n  onToolClick,\n  className,\n}: BenchmarkEvidenceProps) {\n  const [isExpanded, setIsExpanded] = useState(false);\n  const [expandedTools, setExpandedTools] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set());\n\n  if (!benchmarkData || !benchmarkData.results || benchmarkData.results.length === 0) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  const toggleToolExpanded = (toolName: string) => {\n    const newExpanded = new Set(expandedTools);\n    if (newExpanded.has(toolName)) {\n      newExpanded.delete(toolName);\n    } else {\n      newExpanded.add(toolName);\n    }\n    setExpandedTools(newExpanded);\n  };\n\n  const getRankBadgeVariant = (rank: number): \"default\" | \"secondary\" | \"outline\" => {\n    if (rank === 1) return \"default\";\n    if (rank <= 3) return \"secondary\";\n    return \"outline\";\n  };\n\n  const getRankIcon = (rank: number) => {\n    if (rank === 1) return <Trophy className=\"h-3 w-3 text-yellow-500\" />;\n    if (rank === 2) return <Award className=\"h-3 w-3 text-gray-400\" />;\n    if (rank === 3) return <Award className=\"h-3 w-3 text-amber-600\" />;\n    return <span className=\"text-xs font-mono\">{rank}</span>;\n  };\n\n  const formatMetricValue = (value: number | string, unit?: string): string => {\n    if (typeof value === \"number\") {\n      if (value < 0.01) return value.toExponential(2);\n      if (value < 1) return value.toFixed(3);\n      if (value > 1000) return value.toLocaleString();\n      return value.toFixed(2);\n    }\n    return String(value);\n  };\n\n  const bestTool = benchmarkData.best_tool || benchmarkData.winner || benchmarkData.results[0]?.tool_name;\n\n  return (\n    <Card className={cn(\n      \"border-amber-200 dark:border-amber-800 bg-amber-50/50 dark:bg-amber-950/20\",\n      className\n    )}>\n      <CardHeader className=\"pb-3\">\n        <CardTitle className=\"text-sm flex items-center justify-between\">\n          <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2\">\n            <BarChart3 className=\"h-4 w-4\" />\n            Benchmark Evidence\n            <Badge variant=\"outline\" className=\"text-xs\">\n              <Beaker className=\"h-3 w-3 mr-1\" />\n              Validated\n            </Badge>\n          </div>\n          <Button\n            size=\"sm\"\n            variant=\"ghost\"\n            onClick={() => setIsExpanded(!isExpanded)}\n            className=\"h-6 px-2\"\n          >\n            {isExpanded ? (\n              <ChevronDown className=\"h-4 w-4\" />\n            ) : (\n              <ChevronRight className=\"h-4 w-4\" />\n            )}\n          </Button>\n        </CardTitle>\n      </CardHeader>\n\n      <CardContent className=\"space-y-3\">\n        {/* Summary section - always visible */}\n        <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2 p-2 bg-background rounded-lg border\">\n          <Trophy className=\"h-5 w-5 text-yellow-500 flex-shrink-0\" />\n          <div className=\"flex-1 min-w-0\">\n            <p className=\"text-sm font-medium\">\n              Recommended: <span className=\"text-primary\">{bestTool}</span>\n            </p>\n            {benchmarkData.evidence && (\n              <p className=\"text-xs text-muted-foreground truncate\">\n                {benchmarkData.evidence}\n              </p>\n            )}\n            {benchmarkData.recommendation && (\n              <p className=\"text-xs text-muted-foreground\">\n                {benchmarkData.recommendation}\n              </p>\n            )}\n          </div>\n        </div>\n\n        {/* Tool comparison - shown when expanded */}\n        {isExpanded && (\n          <>\n            {/* Study source */}\n            {benchmarkData.study && (\n              <div className=\"p-2 bg-muted/50 rounded-lg text-xs\">\n                <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2 mb-1\">\n                  <BookOpen className=\"h-3 w-3\" />\n                  <span className=\"font-medium\">Source Study</span>\n                </div>\n                <p className=\"text-muted-foreground\">\n                  {benchmarkData.study.study_name}\n                  {benchmarkData.study.year && ` (${benchmarkData.study.year})`}\n                </p>\n                {benchmarkData.study.doi && (\n                  <a\n                    href={`https://doi.org/${benchmarkData.study.doi}`}\n                    target=\"_blank\"\n                    rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n                    className=\"text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400 hover:underline flex items-center gap-1 mt-1\"\n                  >\n                    <ExternalLink className=\"h-3 w-3\" />\n                    DOI: {benchmarkData.study.doi}\n                  </a>\n                )}\n                {benchmarkData.study.pmid && (\n                  <a\n                    href={`https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/${benchmarkData.study.pmid}`}\n                    target=\"_blank\"\n                    rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"\n                    className=\"text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400 hover:underline flex items-center gap-1 mt-1\"\n                  >\n                    <ExternalLink className=\"h-3 w-3\" />\n                    PMID: {benchmarkData.study.pmid}\n                  </a>\n                )}\n              </div>\n            )}\n\n            {/* Tool rankings table */}\n            <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n              <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground\">\n                <TrendingUp className=\"h-3 w-3\" />\n                Tool Rankings\n              </div>\n\n              {benchmarkData.results.slice(0, 5).map((result, index) => {\n                const isToolExpanded = expandedTools.has(result.tool_name);\n                const isBest = result.tool_name === bestTool;\n\n                return (\n                  <div\n                    key={result.tool_name}\n                    className={cn(\n                      \"border rounded-lg p-2 transition-colors\",\n                      isBest\n                        ? \"bg-yellow-50/50 dark:bg-yellow-950/20 border-yellow-200 dark:border-yellow-800\"\n                        : \"bg-background hover:bg-accent/50\"\n                    )}\n                  >\n                    <div className=\"flex items-center justify-between\">\n                      <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2\">\n                        <Badge\n                          variant={getRankBadgeVariant(result.rank)}\n                          className=\"w-6 h-6 p-0 flex items-center justify-center\"\n                        >\n                          {getRankIcon(result.rank)}\n                        </Badge>\n                        <button\n                          onClick={() => toggleToolExpanded(result.tool_name)}\n                          className=\"font-medium text-sm hover:underline text-left\"\n                        >\n                          {result.tool_name}\n                        </button>\n                        {isBest && (\n                          <Badge variant=\"default\" className=\"text-xs\">\n                            Best\n                          </Badge>\n                        )}\n                      </div>\n\n                      <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2\">\n                        <TooltipProvider>\n                          <Tooltip>\n                            <TooltipTrigger asChild>\n                              <Badge variant=\"outline\" className=\"text-xs font-mono\">\n                                {result.metric_name}: {formatMetricValue(result.metric_value, result.metric_unit)}\n                                {result.metric_unit && ` ${result.metric_unit}`}\n                              </Badge>\n                            </TooltipTrigger>\n                            <TooltipContent>\n                              <p className=\"text-xs\">{result.metric_name} performance metric</p>\n                            </TooltipContent>\n                          </Tooltip>\n                        </TooltipProvider>\n\n                        <Button\n                          size=\"sm\"\n                          variant=\"ghost\"\n                          onClick={() => toggleToolExpanded(result.tool_name)}\n                          className=\"h-6 w-6 p-0\"\n                        >\n                          <ChevronRight\n                            className={cn(\n                              \"h-4 w-4 transition-transform\",\n                              isToolExpanded && \"rotate-90\"\n                            )}\n                          />\n                        </Button>\n                      </div>\n                    </div>\n\n                    {/* Expanded tool details */}\n                    {isToolExpanded && (\n                      <div className=\"mt-2 pt-2 border-t space-y-2\">\n                        {result.evidence_text && (\n                          <div className=\"text-xs bg-muted/50 p-2 rounded\">\n                            <div className=\"flex items-start gap-1\">\n                              <Info className=\"h-3 w-3 mt-0.5 flex-shrink-0 text-blue-500\" />\n                              <span>{result.evidence_text}</span>\n                            </div>\n                          </div>\n                        )}\n\n                        {result.context_notes && (\n                          <div className=\"text-xs text-muted-foreground\">\n                            <Zap className=\"h-3 w-3 inline mr-1\" />\n                            {result.context_notes}\n                          </div>\n                        )}\n\n                        {result.galaxy_tool_id && onToolClick && (\n                          <Button\n                            size=\"sm\"\n                            variant=\"outline\"\n                            className=\"text-xs\"\n                            onClick={() => onToolClick(result.tool_name, result.galaxy_tool_id)}\n                          >\n                            <ExternalLink className=\"h-3 w-3 mr-1\" />\n                            View in Galaxy\n                          </Button>\n                        )}\n                      </div>\n                    )}\n                  </div>\n                );\n              })}\n\n              {benchmarkData.results.length > 5 && (\n                <p className=\"text-xs text-muted-foreground text-center\">\n                  + {benchmarkData.results.length - 5} more tools\n                </p>\n              )}\n            </div>\n\n            {/* Tool comparison table (if available) */}\n            {benchmarkData.comparison && Object.keys(benchmarkData.comparison).length > 0 && (\n              <div className=\"mt-3 pt-3 border-t\">\n                <div className=\"flex items-center gap-2 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground mb-2\">\n                  <BarChart3 className=\"h-3 w-3\" />\n                  Detailed Comparison\n                </div>\n                <div className=\"overflow-x-auto\">\n                  <table className=\"w-full text-xs\">\n                    <thead>\n                      <tr className=\"border-b\">\n                        <th className=\"text-left p-1 font-medium\">Tool</th>\n                        {Object.keys(Object.values(benchmarkData.comparison)[0] || {}).map((metric) => (\n                          <th key={metric} className=\"text-right p-1 font-medium\">\n                            {metric}\n                          </th>\n                        ))}\n                      </tr>\n )}\n          </>\n        )}\n\n        {/* Expand hint when collapsed */}\n        {!isExpanded && benchmarkData.results.length > 1 && (\n          <button\n            onClick={() =>  Show {benchmarkData.results.length} ranked tools and evidence\n          </button>\n        )}\n      </CardContent>\n    </Card>\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Research Response Component\n *\n * Displays                 enhanced_query,
                max_results // 2,
                min_date=f"{min_year}/01/01"
            ),
            self.semantic_scholar.search(
                query,
                max_results // 2,
                year_range=(min_year, current_year),
                fields_of_study=["Biology", "Computer Science"]
            ),
        ]

        results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)

        all_citations = []
        for result in results:
            if isinstance(result, list):
                all_citations.extend(result)

        # Deduplicate and sort
        seen = set()
        unique = []
        for citation in all_citations:
            key = citation.doi or citation.pmid or citation.title
            if key and key not in seen:
                seen.add(key)
                unique.append(citation)

        unique.sort(key=lambda c: (c.year or 0, c.citation_count), reverse=True)

        return unique[:max_results]


# Factory function
def create_literature_client(
    pubmed_api_key: Optional[str] = None,
    s2_api_key: Optional[str] = None
) -> UnifiedLiteratureClient:
    """Create a UnifiedLiteratureClient instance."""
    return UnifiedLiteratureClient(
        pubmed_api_key=pubmed_api_key,
        s2_api_key=s2_api_key
    )
```

## Benchmark Collection Plan Complete

I've created a comprehensive plan at `/backend/20251230_COMPREHENSIVE_BENCHMARK_COLLECTION_PLAN.md`.

### Key Findings

**Database Current State:**
- Galaxy AI Tools DB: 8,095 tools
- tool_knowledge table: 1,627 entries with citations
- BioMate tools: 286 XML tools (21 domains)
- nf-core modules: 335 (213 with DOIs)

**Critical Issues Identified:**

| Tool | Problem | Wrong Citation |
|------|---------|----------------|
| **DIA-NN** | Wrong paper | Cites 2006 DiANNA (disulfide bonds) instead of Demichev 2020 |
| **MetaPhlAn** | Wrong paper | Cites underwater laser scanner (Opt Express) instead of Beghini 2021 |
| **Bracken** | Wrong paper | Cites Danish medical journal instead of Lu 2017 |
| **AlphaFold3** | Missing | Not in database |
| **AlphaFold** | Empty citation | No citation in tools table |

### Plan Summary (6 Phases)

1. **Citation Validation** - Fix wrong citations using automated detection
2. **BioMate Tools** - Collect citations for 286 tools across 21 domains
3. **nf-core Integration** - Map 213 existing DOIs, find 122 missing
4. **Auto-Update Tools** - Add citations for foldseek, htslib, MMseqs2, samtools
5. **Modern Tools** - Add AlphaFold3, DIA-NN v1.8+, Cellpose 2.0, scVI-tools, etc.
6. **Benchmark Papers** - Collect comparison studies (RNA-seq, proteomics, single-cell)

**Appendix D includes correct citations** ready to apply for the wrongly cited tools like DIA-NN, MetaPhlAn, Bracken, AlphaFold, and AlphaFold3.

added = 0\n\n    for domain, papers in DOMAIN_BENCHMARKS.items():\n        for paper in papers:\n            tools = paper.get(\"tools_compared\", [])\n\n            for tool_name in tools:\n                # Check if tool exists\n                cursor.execute(\n                    \"SELECT tool_name, benchmark_papers FROM tool_knowledge WHERE tool_name = ?\",\n                    (tool_name,)\n                )\n                row = cursor.fetchone()\n\n                if not row:\n                    continue\n\n                # Get existing benchmarks\n                existing = []\n                if row[1]:\n                    try:\n                        existing = json.loads(row[1])\n                    except:\n                        existing = []\n\n                # Check if ## 🤖 Message 945 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2025-12-31T23:37:26.689Z*

Excellent observation. Yes, Galaxy and Nextflow workflows are absolutely procedural knowledge - but in a different form:

**Comparison of Knowledge Representations:**

| Aspect | Claude Skills (SKILL.md) | Galaxy/Nextflow Workflows |
|--------|-------------------------|---------------------------|
| Format | Human-readable markdown | Machine-executable (XML/DSL) |
| Consumer | LLMs / Humans | Execution engines |
| Content | HOW to use + WHY | WHAT to execute + ORDER |
| Parameters | Guidelines with rationale | Concrete values per scenario |
| Encoding | Natural language | Structured code |

**What workflows encode that's valuable:**

1. **Expert tool chaining** - which tools work well together (e.g., STAR → featureCounts → DESeq2)
2. **Validated parameter sets** - the 397 Biomni workflows contain tested parameter combinations
3. **Data flow patterns** - how outputs connect to inputs
4. **Domain-specific pipelines** - e.g., RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, proteomics pipelines

**The gap:**

- Workflows show **WHAT** to do (executable recipe)
- Skills explain **WHY** and provide context (educational)
- Neither fully captures **WHEN** to choose one approach over another

**Potential integration:**

```
Workflows (executable)  ←→  Database (decision knowledge)  ←→  Skills (educational)
     ↓                            ↓                              ↓
"Run STAR with these      "Use STAR when read depth     "STAR parameters: use
 params, then DESeq2"      >10M, use kallisto for        --alignIntronMax 50000
                           speed-sensitive cases"         for long introns..."
```

Should we extract procedural knowledge from your 397 Biomni workflows into the benchmark/knowledge database? The workflows already contain validated parameter settings and tool combinations that represent domain expertise.

## 🤖 Message 948 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2025-12-31T23:42:28.094Z*

This is a fundamental architecture question. Let me analyze critically:

**What BioMate DB does well (that Skills can't):**

| Capability | DB Approach | Skills Approach |
|------------|-------------|-----------------|
| Query across 8000+ tools | `SELECT * WHERE domain='proteomics'` | Load 8000 files? No. |
| Rank/compare tools | `ORDER BY benchmark_score DESC` | Can't aggregate |
| Join relationships | Tools ↔ Benchmarks ↔ Workflows | No relational queries |
| Structured decision rules | `IF read_depth < 10M THEN use kallisto` | Buried in prose |

**What Skills do better (that DB can't):**

| Capability | Skills Approach | DB Approach |
|------------|-----------------|-------------|
| Nuanced edge cases | "When you see X, but also Y, consider Z because..." | Doesn't fit schema |
| Code examples with context | Full script with inline explanations | Fragmented |
| Troubleshooting narratives | Step-by-step debugging | Too unstructured |
| Evolving best practices | Easy to update prose | Schema migrations |

**My assessment for BioMate:**

```
User Query
    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DECISION PHASE (DB is better)                           │
│ - Which tool? Query benchmark_results, decision_rules   │
│ - What parameters? Query parameter_recommendations      │
│ - Alternatives? Query tool_knowledge.alternatives       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ EXECUTION PHASE (Workflows are better)                  │
│ - Run validated Galaxy/Nextflow pipelines               │
│ - Parameters already encoded in workflow                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ EXPLANATION PHASE (Skills might help)                   │
│ - Deep troubleshooting                                  │
│ - Complex result interpretation                         │
│ - Edge case handling                                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Efficiency impact:**

- **Adding Skills**: More tokens per request = slower + more expensive
- **Current DB approach**: Minimal tokens, only query what's needed
- **Workflows**: Zero LLM tokens for execution logic

**My recommendation:**

Skills are **redundant** for BioMate because:
1. Your DB already has `scientific_context` with structured know-how
2. Your 397 workflows encode validated procedures
3. Loading skill files adds latency without clear benefit

**What Skills could uniquely provide** (if we wanted them):
- Post-execution result interpretation guides
- Troubleshooting complex failures
- Educational content for users learning tools

But these are **optional enhancements**, not core to the workflow. The DB + Workflow architecture is more efficient for automated scientific analysis.

Do you agree, or do you see a use case where Skills would change BioMate's efficiency?

| **Common pitfalls** | "Don't use X when Y" | `CorrectionLog` (user-specific) | No global pitfalls aggregation |
| **Procedural steps** | Step-by-step tutorials | `ProjectProcedure` (project-scoped) | No global procedures |
| **Workflow templates** | Code examples | 3 hardcoded templates | **397 Biomni workflows unused!** |

## Critical Gap: Feedback Loop Missing

```
Current: One-way flow (DB → User)
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│ Global DB   │ ──→ │ User Memory │ ──→ │ Session     │
└─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘

Missing: Promotion from user learning to global knowledge
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│ Global DB   │ ←── │ User Memory │ ←── │ Session     │
└─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘
      ↑                    ↑
      │                    │
 If many users correct same thing, promote to global pitfall
 If ProjectProcedure has high success_rate, promote to global template
```

## My Assessment: Skills vs Your DB

**You DON'T need Skills because:**
1. Your `scientific_context` field already holds domain know-how
2. Your memory system tracks learned procedures
3. Your 397 Biomni workflows encode expert knowledge

**What you DO need:**
1. **Integrate Biomni workflows into WorkflowSearchRAG** (biggest gap!)
2. **Add `interpretation_guidelines` to benchmark_knowledge.db**
3. **Aggregate `CorrectionLog` to global pitfalls** (feedback loop)
4. **Populate more `decision_rules`** (only RNA gLM domain covered)

**Efficiency impact if properly filled:**
- DB approach: Query specific field → minimal tokens
- Skills approach: Load entire document → more tokens

Your architecture is more efficient - the gap is **data population**, not structure.

## 🤖 Message 1025 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2026-01-01T00:14:45.825Z*

Now I understand the situation. Here's the summary:

## Current Workflow Index Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     galaxy_ai_tools.db                                   │
│                                                                          │
│  workflows table (271 workflows)                                         │
│  ├── With FTS index for search                                          │
│  ├── Categorized by domain (variant_calling: 78, genomics: 39, etc.)    │
│  └── Contains workflow_json for execution                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              +
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     JSON Files (951 workflows)                           │
│                                                                          │
│  lib/galaxy/ai/data/workflows/workflow_*.json                           │
│  ├── Loaded into memory by RAGWorkflowRecommender                       │
│  ├── Keyword-based similarity matching                                  │
│  └── Galaxy community workflows                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              +
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     NOT INDEXED as Workflows                             │
│                                                                          │
│  Biomni tools (285 XMLs) - Individual tools, not complete workflows    │
│  nf-core modules (12 .nf) - Nextflow processes, not in workflow DB      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Gaps Identified

1. **Two separate systems not unified**:
   - `WorkflowSearchRAG` (3 templates) - seems deprecated
   - `RAGWorkflowRecommender` (951 JSON) - in-memory, keyword-based
   - `workflows` table (271) - SQLite with FTS

2. **Biomni tools are NOT workflows**:
   - They're 285 individual tool XMLs
   - No pre-built workflow pipelines combining these tools
   - Need to be composed into workflows at runtime

3. **No unified search across all sources**:
   - DB search and JSON RAG are separate
   - Memory system (`ProjectProcedure`) not linked to workflow index

**Question for you**: Should the Biomni tools be converted into complete workflow templates, or is the current approach (compose at runtime based on user intent) the intended design?

Populate FTS index\n        cursor.execute(\"\"\"\n            INSERT INTO workflows_fts(rowid, name, description, annotation, tags, domain, tools_used)\n            SELECT id, name, description, annotation, tags, domain, tools_used FROM workflows\n        \"\"\")\n\n        conn.commit()\n        log.info(\"FTS index created and populated\")\n\n    def search(self,\n               query: str,\n               domain: Optional[str] = None,\n               source: Optional[str] = None,\n               format: Optional[str] = None,\n               limit: int = 10,\n               include_workflow_json: bool = False) -> List[WorkflowMatch]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Search for workflows matching the query.\n\n        Args:\n            query: Natural language search query\n            domain: Filter by domain (genomics, proteomics, etc.)\n            source: Filter by source (nfcore, biomni, etc.)\n            format: Filter by format (galaxy_ga, nextflow)\n            limit: Maximum results to return\n            include_workflow_json: Include full workflow JSON in results\n\n        Returns:\n            List of WorkflowMatch objects sorted by relevance\n        \"\"\"\n        conn = self._get_connection()\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n\n        try:\n            # Build FTS query\n            fts_query = self._build_fts_query(query)\n\n            # Build SQL with filters\n            sql = \"\"\"\n                SELECT w.id, w.name, w.description, w.domain, w.source, w.format,\n                       w.step_count, w.tools_used, w.tags, w.filename, w.workflow_json,\n                       bm25(workflows_fts) as fts_score\n                FROM workflows w\n                JOIN workflows_fts ON w.id = workflows_fts.rowid\n                WHERE workflows_fts MATCH ?\n            \"\"\"\n            params = [fts_query]\n\n            if domain:\n                sql += \" AND w.domain = ?\"\n                params.append(domain)\n\n            if source:\n                sql += \" AND w.source = ?\"\n                params.append(source)\n\n            if format:\n                sql += \" AND w.format = ?\"\n                params.append(format)\n\n            sql += \" ORDER BY fts_score LIMIT ?\"\n            params.append(limit * 3)  # Get more for re-ranking\n\n            cursor.execute(sql, params)\n            rows = cursor.fetchall()\n\n            # Re-rank with custom scoring\n            results = []\n            for row in rows:\n                match = self._create_match(row, query, include_workflow_json)\n                results.append(match)\n\n            # Sort by custom score (includes source priority)\n            results.sort(key=lambda x: x.score, reverse=True)\n\n            return results[:limit]\n\n        except sqlite3.OperationalError as e:\n            log.warning(f\"FTS search failed: {e}, falling back to LIKE search\")\n            return self._fallback_search(query, domain, source, format, limit, include_workflow_json)\n\n        finally:\n            conn.close()\n\n    def _build_fts_query(self, query: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Build FTS5 query from natural language.\"\"\"\n        # Clean and tokenize\n        words = query.lower().replace(\"-\", \" \").split()\n\n        # Remove common words\n        stopwords = {'i', 'want', 'to', 'the', 'a', 'an', 'for', 'with', 'and', 'or', 'from', 'in', 'on'}\n        words = [w for w in words if w not in stopwords and len(w) > 2]\n\n        # Build OR query for flexibility\n        if words:\n            return \" OR \".join(words)\n        return query\n\n    def _create_match(self, row: tuple, query: str, include_json: bool) -> WorkflowMatch:\n        \"\"\"Create WorkflowMatch from database row.\"\"\"\n        id_, name, description, domain, source, format_, step_count, tools_json, tags_json, filename, workflow_json, fts_score = row\n\n        # Parse JSON fields\n        try:\n            tools = json.loads(tools_json) if tools_json else []\n        except:\n            tools = []\n\n        try:\n            tags = json.loads(tags_json) if tags_json else []\n        except:\n            tags = []\n\n        # Calculate custom score\n        score = self._calculate_score(query, name, description or \"\", tools, tags, source, fts_score)\n        match_type = self._classify_match(score)\n\n        return WorkflowMatch(\n            id=id_,\n            name=name,\n            description=description or \"\",\n            domain=domain or \"general\",\n            source=source or \"unknown\",\n            format=format_ or \"galaxy_ga\",\n            step_count=step_count or 0,\n            tools=tools,\n            tags=tags,\n            score=score,\n            match_type=match_type,\n            filename=filename,\n            workflow_json=workflow_json if include_json else None\n        )\n\n    def _calculate_score(self,\n                         query: str,\n                         name: str,\n                         description: str,\n                         tools: List[str],\n                         tags: List[str],\n                         source: str,\n                         fts_score: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Calculate relevance score with source priority.\"\"\"\n        score = 0.0\n        query_lower = query.lower()\n        text = f\"{name} {description} {' '.join(tools)} {' '.join(tags)}\".lower()\n\n        # 1. FTS score (normalized, ~40% weight)\n        score += abs(fts_score) * 2.0\n\n        # 2. Keyword matching (~30% weight)\n        for keyword, weight in self.keyword_weights.items():\n            if keyword in query_lower and keyword in text:\n                score += weight\n\n        # 3. Name match bonus (~20% weight)\n        query_words = set(query_lower.split())\n        name_words = set(name.lower().split())\n        overlap = len(query_words.intersection(name_words))\n        score += overlap * 2.0\n\n        # 4. Source priority (~10% weight)\n        source_bonus = SOURCE_PRIORITY.get(source, 0) / 50.0  # Normalize to ~2.0 max\n        score += source_bonus\n\n        return round(score, 2)\n\n    def _classify_match(self, score: float) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Classify match confidence.\"\"\"\n        if score >= 8.0:\n            return \"high_confidence\"\n        elif score >= 4.0:\n            return \"medium_confidence\"\n        else:\n            return \"low_confidence\"\n\n    def _fallback_search(self,\n                         query: str,\n                         domain: Optional[str],\n                         source: Optional[str],\n                         format: Optional[str],\n                         limit: int,\n                         include_json: bool) -> List[WorkflowMatch]:\n        \"\"\"Fallback to LIKE search if FTS fails.\"\"\"\n        conn = self._get_connection()\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n\n        try:\n            sql = \"\"\"\n                SELECT id, name, description, domain, source, format,\n                       step_count, tools_used, tags, filename, workflow_json, 0.0 as fts_score\n                FROM workflows\n                WHERE name LIKE ? OR description LIKE ? OR tools_used LIKE ?\n            \"\"\"\n            like_pattern = f\"%{query}%\"\n            params = [like_pattern, like_pattern, like_pattern]\n\n            if domain:\n                sql += \" AND domain = ?\"\n                params.append(domain)\n\n            if source:\n                sql += \" AND source = ?\"\n                params.append(source)\n\n            if format:\n                sql += \" AND format = ?\"\n                params.append(format)\n\n            sql += \" LIMIT ?\"\n            params.append(limit)\n\n            cursor.execute(sql, params)\n            rows = cursor.fetchall()\n\n            results = []\n            for row in rows:\n                match = self._create_match(row, query, include_json)\n                results.append(match)\n\n            results.sort(key=lambda x: x.score, reverse=True)\n            return results\n\n        finally:\n            conn.close()\n\n    def get_workflow(self, workflow_id: int) -> Optional[WorkflowMatch]:\n        \"\"\"Get a specific workflow by ID.\"\"\"\n        conn = self._get_connection()\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"\"\"\n                SELECT id, name, description, domain, source, format,\n                       step_count, tools_used, tags, filename, workflow_json\n                FROM workflows\n                WHERE id = ?\n            \"\"\", (workflow_id,))\n\n            row = cursor.fetchone()\n            if not row:\n                return None\n\n            # Add dummy fts_score\n            row = row + (0.0,)\n            return self._create_match(row, \"\", True)\n\n        finally:\n            conn.close()\n\n    def get_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Get workflow index statistics.\"\"\"\n        conn = self._get_connection()\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM workflows\")\n            total = cursor.fetchone()[0]\n\n            cursor.execute(\"SELECT source, COUNT(*) FROM workflows GROUP BY source\")\n            by_source = dict(cursor.fetchall())\n\n            cursor.execute(\"SELECT domain, COUNT(*) FROM workflows GROUP BY domain ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 10\")\n            by_domain = dict(cursor.fetchall())\n\n            cursor.execute(\"SELECT format, COUNT(*) FROM workflows GROUP BY format\")\n            by_format = dict(cursor.fetchall())\n\n            return {\n                \"total\": total,\n                \"by_source\": by_source,\n                \"by_domain\": by_domain,\n                \"by_format\": by_format\n            }\n\n        finally:\n            conn.close()\n\n    def list_domains(self) -> List[str]:\n        \"\"\"List all available domains.\"\"\"\n        conn = self._get_connection()\n        cursor = conn.cursor()\n\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"SELECT DISTINCT domain FROM workflows WHERE domain IS NOT NULL ORDER BY domain\")\n            return [row[0] for row in cursor.fetchall()]\n

## 🤖 Message 1727 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2026-01-10T01:22:20.879Z*

I misspoke. Let me clarify:

**Most biological databases are public** (UniProt, PDB, KEGG, etc.) - no credentials needed.

**However**, many Biomni database tools use an **LLM-based query interface**:

```python
# LLM-based (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY):
query_kegg(prompt="Find glycolysis pathway in humans")
query_uniprot(prompt="Find insulin protein information")

# Direct API (no LLM needed):
blast_sequence(sequence="ATGC...", database="nr", program="blastn")
```

The tools with `prompt` parameter use Claude to convert natural language → API calls. That's why `query_uniprot` earlier failed with:
```
Error: langchain-anthropic package is required for Anthropic models
```

**To use LLM-based database tools**, you need:
1. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable set
2. `langchain-anthropic` package in Docker container

**Direct API tools** work without any credentials - they just call public REST APIs.

def get_hpo_names(hpo_terms: list[str], data_lake_path: str) -> list[str]:
    """Retrieve the names of given HPO terms.

    Args:
        hpo_terms (List[str]): A list of HPO terms (e.g., ['HP:0001250']).

    Returns:
        List[str]: A list of corresponding HPO term names.

    """
    hp_dict = parse_hpo_obo(data_lake_path + "/hp.obo")

    hpo_names = []
    for term in hpo_terms:
        name = hp_dict.get(term, f"Unknown term: {term}")
        hpo_names.append(name)
    return hpo_names

Now I have a complete picture. Let me summarize my findings about the LLM support mechanisms in biomni database queries:

---

## Biomni LLM-Based Database Query System Analysis

### 1. Supportive Information Provided to LLM

The LLM receives **comprehensive API schema documentation** stored in pickle files (`schema_db/*.pkl`). For UniProt, this includes:

```json
{
  "base_url": "https://rest.uniprot.org",
  "categories": {
    "UniProtKB": {
      "description": "The UniProt Knowledgebase",
      "endpoints": {
        "GET /uniprotkb/{id}": { "description": "...", "required_params": [...], "example": "..." },
        "GET /uniprotkb/search": { "description": "...", "optional_params": [...] }
      },
      "formats": ["json", "xml", "fasta", ...],
      "entry_pattern": "P\\d{5}"
    }
  },
  "query_fields": {
    "accession": { "description": "...", "example": "accession:P62988" },
    "gene": { "description": "...", "example": "gene:INS" }
  }
}
```

The system also provides **domain-specific hints** in the system prompt:
- "Search in reviewed (Swiss-Prot) entries first"
- "Assume organism is human unless otherwise specified (taxonomy ID: 9606)"
- "Use `gene_exact:` for exact gene name searches"

**33 database schemas** are available covering: UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, PDB, gnomAD, ClinVar, ENCODE, Reactome, and more.

### 2. Validation Mechanisms

**Current validation is minimal**:
- **JSON parsing validation**: Extracts JSON from LLM response (lines 89-97 in `database.py`)
- **Endpoint format validation**: Some functions validate known endpoints (e.g., AlphaFold: `["prediction", "summary", "annotations"]`)
- **Basic parameter checks**: Checks for required parameters like `uniprot_id`

**What's NOT validated**:
- LLM-generated URLs are not pre-validated before API calls
- Query syntax is not checked against schema
- No semantic validation of query logic

### 3. Error Handling

**Basic error handling exists** (`_query_rest_api` function, lines 111-196):
- HTTP status code checking
- Detailed error message extraction from API responses
- Error information returned in structured dict with `success: False`

**Example error response**:
```python
{
    "success": False,
    "error": "API error: ...",
    "query_info": {"endpoint": "...", "method": "GET"},
    "response_url_error": "...",  # Raw API error
}
```

### 4. Retry Logic

**Limited retry logic** - only for specific cases:
- **BLAST searches**: Has `max_attempts = 2` with retry on timeout (lines 2865-2947)
- **Fallback patterns**: Some functions have LLM-based parsing fallbacks (line 4178)

**No automatic retry for**:
- LLM query generation failures
- Invalid URLs generated by LLM
- API rate limiting

### 5. User Interaction for Failed Queries

**Currently: None**. The system has a **fire-and-forget model**:
- If LLM fails to generate valid JSON → returns error dict
- If API returns error → returns error dict  
- No mechanism for:
  - Asking user to clarify query
  - Regenerating query with error feedback
  - Interactive debugging

---

## Recommendations for Improvement

1. **Add query validation layer**: Validate generated URLs against schema before API call
2. **Implement retry with feedback**: Pass API error back to LLM for query refinement
3. **Add user interaction hooks**: Allow failed queries to trigger clarification requests
4. **Implement rate limiting**: Add backoff/retry for API rate limits
5. **Query caching**: Cache successful query patterns for common requests

## 🤖 Message 1979 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2026-01-10T05:00:22.283Z*

## Implementation Complete

I've implemented a comprehensive enhancement to the biomni database query system. Here's what was added:

### New File: `biomni/tool/database_enhanced.py`

**1. Local Database Check (`LocalDatabaseManager`)**
- Scans for local FASTA/PDB files before making API calls
- Supports UniProt FASTA lookups and PDB structure files
- Auto-discovers files in `./data/local_databases/`

**2. Query Validation (`QueryValidator`)**
- Validates LLM-generated URLs against API schemas
- Checks for required parameters
- Reports warnings and errors before API calls

**3. Retry with LLM Feedback**
- Up to 3 retry attempts with error feedback
- Passes API error messages back to LLM for query refinement
- Includes confidence levels in generated queries

**4. User Interaction Hooks**
- Optional `user_interaction_callback` parameter
- Called when all retries fail
- Allows user to provide clarification or direct endpoint

**5. Rate Limiting (`RateLimiter`)**
- Per-database rate limits (e.g., KEGG: 10/min, PubChem: 5/min)
- Exponential backoff on failures
- Minimum interval between requests

**6. Query Caching**
- SQLite-based persistent cache
- Configurable TTL per database (1 week for stable data like UniProt)
- Cache statistics and cleanup functions

### Integration with Existing Code

Modified `database.py` to:
- Import enhanced engine when available
- Added `use_enhanced_query()` wrapper function
- Updated `query_uniprot()` to use enhanced engine with fallback

### Query Flow (Priority Order)

```
1. Check local data files (FASTA, PDB, etc.)
2. Check SQLite cache (if TTL valid)
3. Generate query with LLM + validate
4. Execute API call with rate limiting
5. On failure: retry with error feedback to LLM
6. On all failures: invoke user callback if provided
7. Cache successful results
```

### Test Results

```

  Success: True, Source: api

Query 2: Same endpoint (cached)
  Success: True, Source: cache

Cache stats: 3 queries, 4 accesses
```

Hybrid Cloud-Local Architecture\n**File:** `17_hybrid_cloud_local_architecture.drawio.xml`\n\n**Content:**\n- Workload classification (local vs cloud)\n- Data locality optimization\n- Secure tunnel between local and cloud\n- Cost optimization strategies\n- Failover mechanisms\n\n**Decision Criteria:**\n- Data size: Large datasets stay local, results go to cloud\n- Compute intensity: Heavy jobs go to cloud/HPC\n- Latency requirements: Interactive queries stay local\n- Cost: Burst to cloud when local capacity exceeded\n- Compliance: Sensitive data stays on-premises\n\n**Information Flow:**\n- Job Request \u2192 Workload Classifier \u2192 Local Queue OR Cloud Queue\n- Local Execution \u2192 Local Storage \u2192 Sync to Cloud (if needed)\n- Cloud Execution \u2192 Cloud Storage \u2192 Sync to Local (if needed)\n\n**Key Components:**\n- WorkloadClassifier: Decides execution location\n- DataSyncManager: Handles data movement between environments\n- HybridJobScheduler: Unified job queue across environments\n- CostOptimizer: Monitors and optimizes cloud spending\n- SecureTunnel: VPN/SSH tunnel for cloud communication\n\n---\n\n### 18. Infrastructure Abstraction Layer\n**File:** `18_infrastructure_abstraction_layer.drawio.xml`\n\n**Content:**\n- Unified API for all deployment targets\n- Provider-specific adapters\n- Configuration management\n- Secrets management\n- Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/Pulumi)\n\n**Abstraction   "new_string": "---\n\n## Memory & Learning Architecture\n\nBioMate implements a sophisticated agentic memory system that enables the AI to learn from user interactions and improve over time.\n\n### 4-Layer Memory Hierarchy\n\n| Layer | Storage | TTL | Access Time | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|-----|-------------|---------|\n| L1 Volatile | In-Memory | 5 min | <1ms | Hot session data cache |\n| L2 Transient | Redis | 24 hours | ~5ms | Sessions, temporary state |\n| L3 Persistent | PostgreSQL LTM | Permanent | ~10-50ms | Long-term memory (10 tables) |\n| L4 Searchable | SQLite + Vector | Permanent | ~20-100ms | FTS5 + 384-dim embeddings |\n\n**Key Files:**\n- `frontend/server/cache.ts` - L1 in-memory cache\n- `frontend/server/redis-session.ts` - L2 Redis sessions\n- `frontend/shared/ltm-schema.ts` - L3 LTM database schema\n- `backend/lib/galaxy/tools/search_index.py` - L4 hybrid search\n\n### Long-Term Memory Database (10 Tables)\n\n| Domain | Tables | Purpose |\n|--------|--------|---------|\n| User | ltm_users, user_preferences, correction_log | User profiles, learned preferences, explicit corrections |\n| Project | projects, project_knowledge, workflows | Project context, accumulated knowledge, saved workflows |\n| Session | sessions, conversation_messages | Conversation history, message storage |\n| Learning | project_episodes, project_procedures | Episodic memory, emergent procedural knowledge |\n\n### 3 Learning Mechanisms\n\n1. **Explicit Learning**: User corrections are stored with high importance (0.8) in `correction_log`\n2. **Implicit Learning**: Repeated tool/workflow selections increase confidence (+0.1) in `user_preferences`\n3. **Emergent Learning**: 3+ similar episodes trigger automatic procedure generation in `project_procedures`\n\n### AI Tool Search (Hybrid)\n\n```\nQuery \u2192 Parallel Search \u2192 Score Fusion \u2192 Top-K Results\n         \u251c\u2500 SQLite FTS5 (BM25 ranking)\n         \u2514\u2500 Vector (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim)\n\ncombined_score = 0.6 \u00d7 bm25_score + 0.4 \u00d7 cosine_similarity\n```\n\n**Architecture Diagrams:** See `docs/architecture/19-24_*.drawio.xml` for detailed visualizations.\n\n---\n\n## Security Architecture"
}
