  "content": "# Database Schemas\n\nThis document provides comprehensive documentation of all database schemas in the Biomate platform.\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\nBiomate uses multiple databases organized in a 4-layer memory hierarchy:\n\n| Layer | Database | Purpose | Schema File |\n|-------|----------|---------|-------------|\n| L1 | In-Memory | Hot session cache | `frontend/server/cache.ts` |\n| L2 | Redis | Sessions, temp state | `frontend/server/redis-session.ts` |\n| L3 | PostgreSQL | Main app + LTM | `frontend/shared/schema.ts`, `frontend/shared/ltm-schema.ts` |\n| L4 | SQLite | Tool search index | `backend/lib/galaxy/tools/search_index.py` |\n\n**Architecture Diagrams:** See `docs/architecture/19-24_*.drawio.xml` for visual representations.\n\n---\n\n## Main Application Schema (PostgreSQL)\n\n### users\n\nPrimary user account table with authentication, subscription, and Galaxy integration.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE users (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  email         VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,\n  password      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n  full_name     VARCHAR(255),\n\n  -- Authentication\n  email_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,\n  verification_token VARCHAR(255),\n  reset_token   VARCHAR(255),\n  reset_token_expires TIMESTAMP,\n\n  -- Subscription (Stripe integration)\n  subscription_status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'trialing',\n  subscription_tier   VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'free',\n  stripe_customer_id  VARCHAR(255),\n  stripe_subscription_id VARCHAR(255),\n  trial_ends_at TIMESTAMP,\n\n  -- Galaxy Integration\n  galaxy_user_id VARCHAR(255),\n  galaxy_api_key VARCHAR(255),  -- Encrypted at rest\n\n  -- AI Personalization\n  workflow_preferences JSONB DEFAULT '{}',\n  progressive_tuning   JSONB DEFAULT '{}',\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  last_login TIMESTAMP\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);\nCREATE INDEX idx_users_stripe_customer ON users(stripe_customer_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_users_galaxy_user ON users(galaxy_user_id);\n```\n\n**Key Fields:**\n- `workflow_preferences`: User's preferred tools, parameters, output formats\n- `progressive_tuning`: Learned AI behavior adjustments based on feedback\n\n---\n\n### audit_logs\n\nSOC 2 / HIPAA compliant audit trail for all user actions.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE audit_logs (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  user_id       INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),\n\n  -- Action Details\n  action        VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,  -- 'login', 'workflow_run', 'data_access'\n  resource_type VARCHAR(100),           -- 'workflow', 'dataset', 'project'\n  resource_id   VARCHAR(255),\n\n  -- Request Context\n  ip_address    VARCHAR(45),\n  user_agent    TEXT,\n  request_body  JSONB,    -- Sensitive fields redacted\n  response_code INTEGER,\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indexes for compliance queries\nCREATE INDEX idx_audit_user ON audit_logs(user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_audit_action ON audit_logs(action);\nCREATE INDEX idx_audit_created ON audit_logs(created_at);\nCREATE INDEX idx_audit_resource ON audit_logs(resource_type, resource_id);\n```\n\n---\n\n### workflow_executions\n\nTracks Galaxy workflow invocations and their status.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE workflow_executions (\n  id                  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  user_id             INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),\n  ltm_workflow_id     INTEGER REFERENCES ltm_workflows(id),\n\n  -- Galaxy References\n  galaxy_workflow_id    VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n  galaxy_invocation_id  VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n  galaxy_history_id     VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n\n  -- Execution State\n  status            VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending, running, ok, error\n  input_parameters  JSONB,\n  step_states       JSONB,      -- Per-step status tracking\n\n  -- Timing\n  started_at        TIMESTAMP,\n  completed_at      TIMESTAMP,\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at        TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at        TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_executions_user ON workflow_executions(user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_executions_status ON workflow_executions(status);\nCREATE INDEX idx_executions_galaxy ON workflow_executions(galaxy_invocation_id);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Long-Term Memory Schema (PostgreSQL)\n\nThe LTM schema stores the agentic memory system data. It's defined in `frontend/shared/ltm-schema.ts` using Drizzle ORM.\n\n### ltm_users\n\nExtends main users table with LTM-specific metadata.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE ltm_users (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  user_id       INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) UNIQUE,\n\n  -- Memory Configuration\n  memory_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,\n  memory_retention_days INTEGER DEFAULT 365,\n\n  -- Learning Settings\n  explicit_learning_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,\n  implicit_learning_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,\n  emergent_learning_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n```\n\n---\n\n### user_preferences\n\nStores learned user preferences (implicit learning).\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE user_preferences (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  ltm_user_id   INTEGER REFERENCES ltm_users(id),\n\n  -- Preference Details\n  category      VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,  -- 'tool_preference', 'parameter_default', 'output_format'\n  key           VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n  value         TEXT NOT NULL,\n\n  -- Learning Metrics\n  confidence    DECIMAL(3,2) DEFAULT 0.50,  -- 0.00 to 1.00\n  frequency     INTEGER DEFAULT 1,           -- Selection count\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n  UNIQUE(ltm_user_id, category, key)\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_prefs_user ON user_preferences(ltm_user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_prefs_category ON user_preferences(category);\nCREATE INDEX idx_prefs_confidence ON user_preferences(confidence DESC);\n```\n\n**Confidence Scoring:**\n- Initial: 0.50\n- Each repeated selection: +0.10\n- User correction away: -0.20\n- Maximum: 1.00\n\n---\n\n### correction_log\n\nStores explicit user corrections (explicit learning).\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE correction_log (\n  id                  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  ltm_user_id         INTEGER REFERENCES ltm_users(id),\n\n  -- Correction Details\n  context             TEXT NOT NULL,           -- What was the user trying to do\n  original_suggestion TEXT NOT NULL,           -- What AI suggested\n  corrected_value     TEXT NOT NULL,           -- What user corrected to\n  correction_type     VARCHAR(100),            -- 'tool_selection', 'parameter', 'workflow_step'\n\n  -- Learning Weight\n  importance_score    DECIMAL(3,2) DEFAULT 0.80,  -- Explicit corrections weighted highly\n\n  -- Metadata\n  metadata            JSONB DEFAULT '{}',\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at          TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_corrections_user ON correction_log(ltm_user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_corrections_type ON correction_log(correction_type);\nCREATE INDEX idx_corrections_created ON correction_log(created_at DESC);\n```\n\n---\n\n### projects\n\nUser projects with associated context and knowledge.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE projects (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  ltm_user_id   INTEGER REFERENCES ltm_users(id),\n\n  -- Project Info\n  name          VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n  description   TEXT,\n  domain        VARCHAR(100),  -- 'genomics', 'proteomics', 'pharmacology', etc.\n\n  -- Status\n  status        VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'active',\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_projects_user ON projects(ltm_user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_projects_domain ON projects(domain);\nCREATE INDEX idx_projects_status ON projects(status);\n```\n\n---\n\n### project_knowledge\n\nAccumulated knowledge about a project (datasets, organisms, parameters).\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE project_knowledge (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  project_id    INTEGER REFERENCES projects(id),\n\n  -- Knowledge Entry\n  knowledge_type VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,  -- 'dataset_info', 'organism', 'parameter_set'\n  key           VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n  content       JSONB NOT NULL,\n\n  -- Confidence\n  confidence    DECIMAL(3,2) DEFAULT 0.70,\n  source        VARCHAR(100),  -- 'user_stated', 'inferred', 'file_metadata'\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n  UNIQUE(project_id, knowledge_type, key)\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_knowledge_project ON project_knowledge(project_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_knowledge_type ON project_knowledge(knowledge_type);\n```\n\n---\n\n### workflows (LTM)\n\nSaved workflow definitions with success tracking.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE ltm_workflows (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  project_id    INTEGER REFERENCES projects(id),\n\n  -- Workflow Definition\n  name          VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n  description   TEXT,\n  definition    JSONB NOT NULL,         -- Galaxy .ga format\n  tags          TEXT[],\n\n  -- Success Tracking\n  run_count     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,\n  success_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,\n  success_rate  DECIMAL(5,2) DEFAULT 0.00,\n\n  -- Source\n  source        VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT 'ai_generated',  -- 'ai_generated', 'user_created', 'biomni'\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_ltm_workflows_project ON ltm_workflows(project_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_ltm_workflows_success ON ltm_workflows(success_rate DESC);\nCREATE INDEX idx_ltm_workflows_tags ON ltm_workflows USING GIN(tags);\n```\n\n---\n\n### sessions\n\nConversation sessions for context management.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE sessions (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  ltm_user_id   INTEGER REFERENCES ltm_users(id),\n  project_id    INTEGER REFERENCES projects(id),\n\n  -- Session State\n  status        VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'active',\n\n  -- Context Summary\n  summary       TEXT,                    -- LLM-generated session summary\n  key_entities  JSONB DEFAULT '[]',      -- Extracted entities (genes, tools, datasets)\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  ended_at      TIMESTAMP\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_sessions_user ON sessions(ltm_user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_sessions_project ON sessions(project_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_sessions_status ON sessions(status);\n```\n\n---\n\n### conversation_messages\n\nIndividual messages within sessions.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE conversation_messages (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  session_id    INTEGER REFERENCES sessions(id),\n\n  -- Message Content\n  role          VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,    -- 'user', 'assistant', 'system'\n  content       TEXT NOT NULL,\n\n  -- Metadata\n  metadata      JSONB DEFAULT '{}',      -- tool_calls, tokens, thinking_content\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_messages_session ON conversation_messages(session_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_messages_role ON conversation_messages(role);\nCREATE INDEX idx_messages_created ON conversation_messages(created_at);\n```\n\n---\n\n### project_episodes\n\nEpisodic memory - specific interaction instances for emergent learning.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE project_episodes (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  project_id    INTEGER REFERENCES projects(id),\n  session_id    INTEGER REFERENCES sessions(id),\n\n  -- Episode Content\n  trigger       TEXT NOT NULL,           -- What triggered this episode\n  action        TEXT NOT NULL,           -- What action was taken\n  outcome       VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,    -- 'success', 'failure', 'partial'\n\n  -- Learning Metrics\n  confidence    DECIMAL(3,2) DEFAULT 0.70,\n\n  -- Metadata\n  context       JSONB DEFAULT '{}',      -- Additional context\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_episodes_project ON project_episodes(project_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_episodes_outcome ON project_episodes(outcome);\nCREATE INDEX idx_episodes_trigger ON project_episodes USING GIN(to_tsvector('english', trigger));\n```\n\n---\n\n### project_procedures\n\nEmergent procedural knowledge - automatically generated from repeated episodes.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE project_procedures (\n  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  project_id    INTEGER REFERENCES projects(id),\n\n  -- Procedure Definition\n  name          VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n  description   TEXT,\n  trigger_pattern TEXT NOT NULL,          -- Pattern that triggers this procedure\n  steps         JSONB NOT NULL,           -- Ordered list of steps\n\n  -- Source Episodes\n  source_episode_ids INTEGER[],           -- Episodes that generated this\n\n  -- Metrics\n  success_rate  DECIMAL(5,2) DEFAULT 0.00,\n  usage_count   INTEGER DEFAULT 0,\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  created_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indexes\nCREATE INDEX idx_procedures_project ON project_procedures(project_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_procedures_trigger ON project_procedures USING GIN(to_tsvector('english', trigger_pattern));\nCREATE INDEX idx_procedures_success ON project_procedures(success_rate DESC);\n```\n\n**Emergent Learning Rule:** When 3+ similar episodes share a trigger pattern, automatically generate a procedure.\n\n---\n\n## AI Tool Database (SQLite)\n\n### tools\n\nMain tool metadata table.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE tools (\n  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  name          TEXT NOT NULL,\n  description   TEXT,\n\n  -- Classification\n  section       TEXT,                     -- Tool section in Galaxy\n  panel_section TEXT,                     -- Panel section path\n\n  -- Tool Details\n  version       TEXT,\n  repository    TEXT,                     -- ToolShed repository\n\n  -- Search Optimization\n  keywords      TEXT,                     -- Extracted keywords\n\n  -- Timestamps\n  indexed_at    TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n```\n\n### tools_fts\n\nFull-text search virtual table using FTS5.\n\n```sql\nCREATE VIRTUAL TABLE tools_fts USING fts5(\n  id,\n  name,\n  description,\n  keywords,\n  content='tools',\n  content_rowid='rowid',\n  tokenize='porter unicode61'\n);\n```\n\n**BM25 Ranking:** SQLite FTS5 provides built-in BM25 ranking for relevance scoring.\n\n### Vector Embeddings\n\nTool embeddings are stored separately in NPZ format for semantic search.\n\n| Component | Details |\n|-----------|---------|\n| Model | all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (sentence-transformers) |\n| Dimensions | 384 |\n| Storage | `tools_embeddings.npz` |\n| Index | Approximate nearest neighbor (optional FAISS) |\n\n**Hybrid Search Formula:**\n```\ncombined_score = 0.6 * bm25_score + 0.4 * cosine_similarity\n```\n\n---\n\n##

CRITICAL GAP\n\n**Current State**: `email-service.ts` only handles:\n- `sendVerificationEmail()`\n- `sendPasswordResetEmail()`\n- `sendWelcomeEmail()`\n\n**Missing**: No `sendWorkflowCompletedEmail()` or `sendWorkflowErrorEmail()`\n\n**Fix Required**:\n\n```typescript\n// Add to email-service.ts\nasync sendWorkflowCompletedEmail(\n  email: string, userName: string, workflowName: string,\n  invocationId: string, outputsUrl: string\n): Promise<boolean>\n\nasync sendWorkflowErrorEmail(\n  email: string, userName: string, workflowName: string,\n  invocationId: string, errorMessage: string\n): Promise<boolean>\n\n// Connect to galaxy-state-poller.ts\nthis.on('workflow_completed', async (data) => {\n  await emailService.sendWorkflowCompletedEmail(...);\n});\n```\n\n**User Preference Fields** (add to schema.ts):\n```typescript\nnotifyOnCompletion: boolean(\"notify_on_completion\").default(true),\nnotifyOnError: boolean(\"notify_on_error\").default(true),\n```\n\n### 4B.3 Team Management - CRITICAL GAP\n\n**Current State**: `schema.ts` only has `organization: text(\"organization\")` - a plain text field\n\n**Galaxy Has**:\n- `managers/groups.py` - Full group CRUD\n- `managers/roles.py` - Role-based access control\n- `api/groups.py` - REST endpoints for team management\n\n**Fix Required**:\n\n```typescript\n// Add to schema.ts\nexport const teams = pgTable(\"teams\", {\n  id: serial(\"id\").primaryKey(),\n  name: text(\"name\").notNull(),\n  galaxyGroupId: text(\"galaxy_group_id\"),  // Link to Galaxy group\n  createdAt: timestamp(\"created_at\").defaultNow(),\n});\n\nexport const teamMembers = pgTable(\"team_members\", {\n  id: serial(\"id\").primaryKey(),\n  teamId: integer(\"team_id\").references(() => teams.id),\n  userId: integer(\"user_id\").references(() => users.id),\n  role: text(\"role\").default(\"member\"),  // owner, admin, member\n});\n```\n\n**Galaxy API Endpoints to Use**:\n- `POST /api/groups` - Create team\n- `PUT /api/groups/{id}/users/{user_id}` - Add member\n- `DELETE /api/groups/{id}/users/{user_id}` - Remove member\n\n### 4B.4 Concurrent Workflow Management - WORKING\n\n**Good News**: `galaxy-state-poller.ts` properly manages multiple concurrent workflows:\n- Uses `Map<string, InvocationPoller>` for tracking\n- 2-second polling interval\n- Emits state change events\n- SSE streaming to browser\n\n**Gap**: No email notification on completion/error (see 4B.2)\n\n### 4B.5 Galaxy Features to Consider for Phase 2\n\n| Feature | Galaxy Endpoint | Use Case |\n|---------|----------------|----------|\n| Interactive Jupyter | `/api/entry_points` | Result exploration |\n| Data Libraries | `/api/libraries` | Shared reference data |\n| Visualizations | `/api/visualizations` | Genome browser, charts |\n| Quotas | `/api/quotas` | Subscription tier limits |\n| Webhooks | `/api/notifications` | Third-party integrations |\n\n### 4B.6 Integration Priority for Launch\n\n**Week 1 (Must Have)**:\n1. Add workflow notification emails (low effort, high impact)\n2. Add user notification preferences\n\n**Week 2 (Should Have)**:\n1. Add team tables to schema\n2. Create Galaxy group sync\n3. Basic team sharing for workflows\n\n**Post-Launch**:\n1. Interactive tools integration\n2. Data library integration\n3. Visualization plugins\n\n---\n\n## PHASE 5: TESTING STRATEGY"

## Summary

### Key Findings

| Feature | Galaxy Status | BioMate Status |
|---------|--------------|----------------|

| **Team Management** | Groups, RBAC, permissions | Only "organization" text field |
| **Interactive Tools** | Jupyter, RStudio, VS Code | NOT USED |
| **Data Libraries** | Shared data repositories | NOT USED |
| **Visualizations** | Plugin-based charts/genome browser | NOT USED |
| **Quotas** | User/group resource limits | NOT USED |

### Critical Gaps Found

1. **Email Notifications** - `email-service.ts` only has auth emails (verification, reset, welcome). No `sendWorkflowCompletedEmail()` or `sendWorkflowErrorEmail()` exists.

2. **Team Management** - `schema.ts` only has `organization: text("organization")` - a plain text field. No team tables, no roles, no permissions despite Galaxy having full RBAC.

3. **Workflow Polling** (GOOD) - `galaxy-state-poller.ts` properly manages concurrent workflows with Map tracking and SSE streaming.

### Documents Created/Updated

   - Added Galaxy Integration Gap Summary to overview
   - Specific fix recommendations with code examples

3. **`docs/00-START-HERE.md`** (UPDATED)
   - Added Galaxy Capabilities Analysis link
   - Updated document status table
   - Fixed auto-update link with timestamp

### Recommended Immediate Actions

**Week 1 (Low Effort, High Impact):**
1. Add `sendWorkflowCompletedEmail()` and `sendWorkflowErrorEmail()` to `email-service.ts`
2. Connect `galaxy-state-poller.ts` events to email service

**Week 2:**

Change line 141\nconst chatMutation = useMutation({\n  mutationFn: async (content: string) => {\n    const response = await fetch('/api/chat', {  // CORRECT\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n      body: JSON.stringify({\n        message: content,\n        context: {\n          previousMessages: displayMessages.slice(-10),\n          // userId: currentUser?.id  // For personalization\n        }\n      })\n    })\n    // ...\n  }\n})\n```\n\n---\n\n## Issue 2: Hardcoded Localhost URLs\n\n**Severity**: HIGH\n**Location**: `frontend/client/src/components/chat-interface.tsx:798`\n\n### Problem\n\n```typescript\n// chat-interface.tsx line 798\nawait fetch(`http://localhost:8081/api/sessions/${chatSession.id}/compress`, {\n  method: 'POST',\n  headers: {\n    'x-api-key': 'a7e9f73a7c25300e222d27c84efb10f6',  // HARDCODED API KEY!\n    'Content-Type': 'application/json'\n  },\n  // ...\n})\n```\n\n### Issues\n\n1. **Hardcoded `localhost:8081`** - Will fail in any environment except local dev\n2. **Hardcoded API key** - Security risk, exposed in client code\n3. **Port mismatch** - Frontend runs on different port than backend\n\n### Fix Required\n\n```typescript\n// Use relative URL (handled by Vite proxy) or environment variable\nawait fetch(`/api/sessions/${chatSession.id}/compress`, {\n  method: 'POST',\n  headers: {\n    'Content-Type': 'application/json'\n    // API key should be handled by backend session, not passed from client\n  },\n  // ...\n})\n```\n\n---\n\n## Issue 3: Two Parallel Chat Architectures\n\n**Severity**: MEDIUM\n**Location**: `routes.ts`, `galaxy-assistant.ts`, `chat-interface.tsx`\n\n### Problem\n\nThere are TWO chat paths that do different things:\n\n**Path A (Full)**: `/api/chat` \u2192 `galaxy-assistant.ts` \u2192 Full hybrid intelligence\n```\nUser Message \u2192 Intent Analysis \u2192 Tool Search \u2192 Dataset RAG \u2192 Workflow Gen \u2192 Response\n```\n\n**Path B (Partial)**: `/api/ai_assistant/generate_workflow` \u2192 Galaxy backend only\n```\nUser Message \u2192 Direct Workflow Generation (no intent, no tools, no datasets)\n```\n\nThe frontend uses **Path B**, missing all the intelligence from **Path A**.\n\n### Fix Required\n\n1. Frontend should use `/api/chat` for all messages\n2. `/api/ai_assistant/generate_workflow` should be internal only\n3. Consolidate to single chat flow\n\n---\n\n## Issue 4: Response Structure Mismatch\n\n**Severity**: HIGH\n**Location**: `chat-interface.tsx:153-227`\n\n### Problem\n\nThe chat interface expects response from `/api/ai_assistant/generate_workflow`:\n\n```typescript\n// Expected from direct workflow endpoint\n{\n  success: boolean;\n  workflow_ga: object;\n  message: string;\n  confidence: number;\n}\n```\n\nBut `/api/chat` returns different structure:\n\n```typescript\n// From /api/chat endpoint\n{\n  response: string;\n  suggestions: string[];\n  workflow: object;\n  thinking_content?: string;\n  metadata: {\n    recommendedTools: [];\n    recommendedDatasets: [];\n    sources: {};\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Fix Required\n\nUpdate chat-interface.tsx to handle `/api/chat` response structure:\n\n```typescript\nonSuccess: (data) => {\n  // Handle /api/chat response format\n  const workflowData = data.workflow?.workflow_ga || data.workflow;\n  const workflowSuccess = !!data.workflow;\n\n  const aiMessage: Message = {\n    id: (Date.now() + 1).toString(),\n    content: data.response,  // Use natural language response\n    role: \"assistant\",\n    timestamp: new Date(),\n    suggestions: data.suggestions || [],\n    metadata: {\n      type: workflowSuccess ? 'workflow' : 'text',\n      workflow: workflowData,\n      recommendedTools: data.metadata?.recommendedTools,\n      recommendedDatasets: data.metadata?.recommendedDatasets,\n      thinking_content: data.thinking_content,\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Issue 5: Missing Authentication Context\n\n**Severity**: MEDIUM\n**Location**: `chat-interface.tsx`\n\n### Problem\n\nChat requests don't include user authentication:\n\n```typescript\n// No auth token passed\nconst response = await fetch('/api/ai_assistant/generate_workflow', {\n  method: 'POST',\n  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n  // Missing: Authorization header\n  body: JSON.stringify({ request_text: content })\n})\n```\n\n### Impact\n\n- Memory integration won't work (requires userId)\n- User patterns/preferences not loaded\n- Workflow history not associated with user\n- Rate limiting may not work correctly\n\n### Fix Required\n\n```typescript\n// Include auth token from context\nconst { token } = useAuth();  // or however auth is managed\n\nconst response = await fetch('/api/chat', {\n  method: 'POST',\n  headers: {\n    'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n    'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`  // Add auth\n  },\n  body: JSON.stringify({\n    message: content,\n    context: {\n      memorySessionId: chatSession?.id,\n      projectId: currentProject?.id,\n    }\n  })\n})\n```\n\n---\n\n## Issue 6: SSE Connection Not Used for Chat\n\n**Severity**: LOW\n**Location**: `useWorkflowExecution.ts`\n\n### Current State\n\nThe SSE (Server-Sent Events) connection is well-implemented for workflow execution:\n- `useWorkflowExecution.ts` connects to `/api/galaxy/workflows/sse/:workflowId/:invocationId`\n- Handles `workflow_state`, `step_state`, `job_log`, `error` events\n- Auto-reconnects on failure\n\n### Missing\n\nSSE is **not used for chat streaming**. All chat responses are synchronous.\n\n### Recommendation\n\nConsider adding streaming chat responses for better UX with long responses:\n\n```typescript\n// Optional enhancement for streaming\nconst eventSource = new EventSource('/api/chat/stream');\neventSource.onmessage = (event) => {\n  appendToResponse(event.data);\n};\n```\n\n---\n\n## Issue 7: Demo Workflow Fallback Confusion\n\n**Severity**: MEDIUM\n**Location**: `chat-interface.tsx:162-181`\n\n### Current Behavior\n\nWhen workflow generation fails, a demo workflow is shown:\n\n```typescript\nif (!data.success || !data.workflow_ga) {\n  workflowData = generateDemoWorkflow();  // Hardcoded RNA-seq workflow\n  isDemo = true;\n}\n```\n\n### Problem\n\nUsers might think the demo workflow is real and try to execute it, causing confusion when it fails or produces wrong results.\n\n### Fix Required\n\n1. Make demo workflows **clearly non-executable**\n2. Disable \"Run\" button for demo workflows\n3. Show prominent \"DEMO - NOT EXECUTABLE\" badge\n\n---\n\n## Issue 8: Galaxy URL Configuration\n\n**Severity**: HIGH\n**Location**: `galaxy-api-proxy.ts:32-33`\n\n### Current State\n\n```typescript\nconstructor(galaxyUrl?: string, apiKey?: string) {\n  this.galaxyUrl = galaxyUrl || process.env.GALAXY_URL || 'http://localhost:8080';\n  this.apiKey = apiKey || process.env.GALAXY_API_KEY;\n}\n```\n\n### Potential Issues\n\n1. **Default localhost** - If `GALAXY_URL` not set, defaults to localhost\n2. **No validation** - Doesn't check if Galaxy is reachable\n3. **API key exposure** - Key might not be set in production\n\n### Fix Required\n\nAdd startup validation:\n\n```typescript\nconstructor(galaxyUrl?: string, apiKey?: string) {\n  this.galaxyUrl = galaxyUrl || process.env.GALAXY_URL;\n  if (!this.galaxyUrl) {\n    throw new Error('GALAXY_URL environment variable is required');\n  }\n\n  this.apiKey = apiKey || process.env.GALAXY_API_KEY;\n  if (!this.apiKey) {\n    console.warn('[GalaxyAPIProxy] No API key configured - some operations will fail');\n  }\n\n  // Validate connection on startup\n  this.validateConnection();\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Fix Priority List\n\n### Must Fix Before Launch\n\n| Priority | Issue | File | Effort |\n|----------|-------|------|--------|\n| 1 | Chat endpoint mismatch | `chat-interface.tsx:141` | Low |\n| 2 | Hardcoded localhost URL | `chat-interface.tsx:798` | Low |\n| 3 | Response structure handling | `chat-interface.tsx:153-227` | Medium |\n| 4 | Add auth to chat requests | `chat-interface.tsx` | Low |\n| 5 | Galaxy URL validation | `galaxy-api-proxy.ts` | Low |\n\n### Should Fix\n\n| Priority | Issue | File | Effort |\n|----------|-------|------|--------|\n| 6 | Demo workflow distinction | `chat-interface.tsx` | Low |\n| 7 | Consolidate chat paths | `routes.ts` | Medium |\n\n### Nice to Have\n\n| Priority | Issue | File | Effort |\n|----------|-------|------|--------|\n| 8 | Streaming chat responses | Multiple | High |\n\n---\n\n## Next Steps\n\n1. **Fix Issue 1 first** - ## 🤖 Message 2517 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2026-01-13T19:50:13.401Z*

I've completed the audit and made several critical fixes. Here's a summary:

## Summary of Fixes Made

### 1. Chat Interface API Endpoint Fix (`chat-interface.tsx`)
**Problem**: Frontend was calling `/api/ai_assistant/generate_workflow` directly, bypassing the full hybrid intelligence system.

**Fix**: Changed to use `/api/chat` which provides:
- Intent analysis with Claude
- Tool search (2,177 indexed tools)
- Dataset RAG (BioMNI)
- Workflow generation with validation
- Natural language response with suggestions

### 2. Hardcoded Localhost URL Fix (`chat-interface.tsx:798`)
**Problem**: Hardcoded `http://localhost:8081/api/sessions/...` with exposed API key.

**Fix**: Changed to relative URL `/api/memory/sessions/...` and wrapped in try-catch to prevent failures from blocking compression.

### 3. Galaxy API Proxy Validation (`galaxy-api-proxy.ts`)
**Problem**: No validation of Galaxy connection, silent failures.

**Fixes**:
- Added startup connection validation
- Added warnings when GALAXY_URL or GALAXY_API_KEY not set
- Increased timeout from 30s to 60s for workflow generation
- Added `validateConnection()` and `getConnectionStatus()` methods

### 4. Enhanced Health Check (`routes.ts`)
**Problem**: Health endpoint only returned "ok".

**Fix**: Now returns detailed status including:
- Galaxy connection status
- AI assistant availability
- Error messages if any

## Documents Created

| Document | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `20260113_GALAXY_CAPABILITIES_ANALYSIS.md` | Comprehensive analysis of Galaxy features (used vs unused) |
| `20260113_FRONTEND_BACKEND_CONNECTION_ISSUES.md` | Detailed issue list with fixes |
| Updated `20260112_SYSTEM_AUDIT_AND_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md` | Added Galaxy integration section |

## Key Remaining Work

1. **Test the fixes** - Run E2E tests to verify chat flow works
2. **Add workflow notifications** - Email on completion/error (critical gap)
3. **Add team tables** - Currently only "organization" text field exists
4. **Review other hardcoded values** - Search for other localhost references

Would you like me to continue with testing the fixes, or focus on implementing the workflow notification feature?

## 1. MEMORY SYSTEMS (Long-Term Memory Architecture)

### Database Schema
**File:** `/home/yzhang/biomate/frontend/shared/ltm-schema.ts`

BioMate implements a sophisticated **10-table database schema** for persistent learning:

#### Core Tables:

| Table | Purpose | Learning Mechanism |
|-------|---------|-------------------|
| **ltm_users** | User profiles & expertise | Tracks expertiseLevel, researchDomain, totalWorkflows, successRate |
| **user_preferences** | Learned tool/parameter preferences | Records preferenceType, confidence, usageCount, learnedFrom source |
| **correction_log** | Learning from mistakes | Stores suggestedApproach vs correctedApproach with userExplanation |
| **project_episodes** | Episodic memory (agentic) | Records interaction outcomes with lessons_learned, whatWorked, whatFailed |
| **project_procedures** | Procedural memory (learned workflows) | Consolidates successful episodes into reusable patterns with successRate |
| **project_knowledge** | Project-specific knowledge base | Domain context, experimental design, technical notes |
| **sessions** | Interaction sessions | Captures full conversation context, summary, keyDecisions |
| **conversation_messages** | Message history | All user-assistant exchanges with toolsUsed metadata |
| **workflows** | Workflow execution history | Tracks domain, dataType, analysisGoal, execution status, success/error |
| **projects** | Project context | primaryDomain, organisms, dataModalities, researchGoal, instructions |

Audit Log Schema\n\n### 2.1 Main Audit Table\n\n```typescript\n// frontend/shared/schema.ts\nexport const auditLogs = pgTable(\"audit_logs\", {\n  id: varchar(\"id\").primaryKey(),\n\n  // WHO\n  userId: text(\"user_id\"),              // null for anonymous\n  sessionId: text(\"session_id\"),\n\n  // WHAT\n  action: text(\"action\").notNull(),     // e.g., \"workflow.execute\"\n  resourceType: text(\"resource_type\"),  // e.g., \"workflow\"\n  resourceId: text(\"resource_id\"),      // e.g., \"wf-12345\"\n\n  // DETAILS\n  details: text(\"details\"),             // JSON context\n  reasoning: text(\"reasoning\"),         // AI decision explanation\n\n  // WHEN\n  timestamp: timestamp(\"timestamp\").defaultNow(),\n\n  // WHERE\n  ipAddress: text(\"ip_address\"),\n  userAgent: text(\"user_agent\"),\n\n  // RESULT\n  status: text(\"status\"),               // \"success\" | \"failure\" | \"error\"\n  errorMessage: text(\"error_message\"),\n  durationMs: text(\"duration_ms\"),\n});\n```\n\n### 2.2 Workflow Executions Table\n\n```typescript\nexport const workflowExecutions = pgTable(\"workflow_executions\", {\n  id: varchar(\"id\").primaryKey(),\n\n  // OWNERSHIP\n  userId: text(\"user_id\").notNull(),\n  projectId: text(\"project_id\"),\n\n  // GALAXY REFERENCES\n  galaxyInvocationId: text(\"galaxy_invocation_id\").notNull(),\n  galaxyWorkflowId: text(\"galaxy_workflow_id\"),\n  galaxyHistoryId: text(\"galaxy_history_id\"),\n\n  // WORKFLOW DETAILS\n  workflowName: text(\"workflow_name\"),\n  workflowDefinition: text(\"workflow_definition\"),  // Full JSON\n\n  // STATUS\n  status: text(\"status\"),                 // new | queued | running | ok | error\n  startedAt: timestamp(\"started_at\"),\n  completedAt: timestamp(\"completed_at\"),\n\n  // PROGRESS\n  totalSteps: text(\"total_steps\"),\n  completedSteps: text(\"completed_steps\"),\n\n  // ERROR TRACKING\n  errorMessage: text(\"error_message\"),\n});\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Audit Service Methods\n\n### 3.1 Authentication Auditing\n\n```typescript\n// frontend/server/audit-service.ts\nawait auditService.logAuth(\n  action: 'login' | 'logout' | 'register' | 'password_reset',\n  userId: string | null,\n  ipAddress: string,\n  userAgent: string,\n  success: boolean,\n  errorMessage?: string\n);\n```\n\n**Logged Actions:**\n- `auth.login` - User login attempts\n- `auth.logout` - User logout\n- `auth.register` - New user registration\n- `auth.password_reset` - Password reset requests\n\n### 3.2 Workflow Auditing\n\n```typescript\n// Workflow Generation\nawait auditService.logWorkflowGeneration(\n  userId: string | null,\n  workflowName: string,\n  toolsUsed: string[],\n  reasoning: string,        // AI decision explanation\n  success: boolean,\n  errorMessage?: string\n);\n\n// Execution Start\nawait auditService.logWorkflowExecutionStart(\n  userId: string | null,\n  invocationId: string,\n  workflowName: string,\n  galaxyHistoryId: string\n);\n\n// Execution Complete\nawait auditService.logWorkflowExecutionComplete(\n  userId: string | null,\n  invocationId: string,\n  status: 'success' | 'failure' | 'error',\n  durationMs: number,\n  errorMessage?: string\n);\n```\n\n### 3.3 Dataset Auditing\n\n```typescript\nawait auditService.logDatasetUpload(\n  userId: string | null,\n  datasetId: string,\n  fileName: string,\n  fileSize: number\n);\n```\n\n### 3.4 Access Control Auditing\n\n```

     export class GalaxyAPIProxy {
       private isConnected: boolean = false;
       private connectionError: string | null = null;

       constructor(galaxyUrl?: string, apiKey?: string) {
         // Added warnings
         if (!process.env.GALAXY_URL) {
           console.warn('[GalaxyAPIProxy] WARNING: GALAXY_URL not set');
         }
         // Increased timeout from 30s to 60s
         timeout: 60000,
         // Validate connection on startup
         this.validateConnection().catch(err => {...});
       }

       async validateConnection(): Promise<{ connected: boolean; error?: string; version?: string }> {
         try {
           const response = await this.client.get('/api/version', { timeout: 10000 });
           this.isConnected = true;
           console.log('[GalaxyAPIProxy] ✅ Connection validated - Galaxy version:', response.data.version_major);
           return { connected: true, version: response.data.version_major };
         } catch (error: any) {
           this.isConnected = false;
           this.connectionError = error.message;
           return { connected: false, error: this.connectionError };
         }
       }

       getConnectionStatus(): { connected: boolean; error: string | undefined; url: string } {
         return {
           connected: this.isConnected,
           error: this.connectionError || undefined,
           url: this.galaxyUrl
         };
       }
     }
     ```

    51→        async for message in client.receive_messages():
    52→            if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage):

     7→# Hooks Configuration
     8→
     9→## Overview
    10→
    11→Hooks are an event-driven mechanism in iFlow CLI that allows you to automatically execute custom commands when specific lifecycle events occur. By configuring Hooks, you can implement automated processing before and after tool calls, environment setup enhancement, cleanup operations when sessions stop, and more.
    12→
    13→### Key Features
    14→
    15→- **Tool Call Interception**: Run custom logic before and after tool execution
    16→- **Environment Enhancement**: Dynamically set environment information when sessions begin
    17→- **Lifecycle Management**: Execute cleanup operations when sessions or subagents stop
    18→- **Flexible Configuration**: Support hierarchical configuration at user and project levels
    19→- **Security Control**: Can block tool execution or modify tool behavior
    20→
    21→## Hook Types
    22→
    23→iFlow CLI supports the following 9 Hook types:
    24→
    25→### 1. PreToolUse Hook
    26→**Trigger Time**: Before tool execution
    27→**Use Cases**:
    28→- Validate tool parameters
    29→- Set execution environment
    30→- Log tool calls
    31→- Block unsafe operations
    32→
    33→**Example Configuration**:
    34→```json
    35→{
    36→  "hooks": {
    37→    "PreToolUse": [
    38→      {
    39→        "matcher": "Edit",
    40→        "hooks": [
    41→          {
    42→            "type": "command",
    43→            "command": "echo 'File edit detected'"
    44→          }
    45→        ]
    46→      }
    47→    ]
    48→  }
    49→}
    50→```
    51→
    52→### 2. PostToolUse Hook
    53→**Trigger Time**: After tool execution
    54→**Use Cases**:
    55→- Process tool execution results
    56→- Clean up temporary files
    57→- Send n...

    11→
    12→iFlow CLI uses a layered configuration system that takes effect in the following priority order, with higher priority settings overriding lower priority settings:
    13→
    14→1. Application Defaults: CLI built-in basic configuration
    15→2. User Global Settings: Your personal default configuration, applies to all projects
    16→3. Project-Specific Settings: Configuration for specific projects, overrides user settings
    17→4. System-Level Settings: Administrator configuration, applies to the entire system
    18→5. Command Line Parameters: Temporary configuration specified at startup, highest priority

    21→
    22→iFlow CLI now supports configuration through environment variables. **All configuration items in `~/.iflow/settings.json` can be set through environment variables with the IFLOW\_ prefix**, avoiding conflicts with environment variables from other projects.

    27→

    29→
    30→For any configuration item in `settings.json`, iFlow supports the following 4 environment variable naming conventions (sorted by priority):
    31→
    32→1. **IFLOW\_ prefixed camelCase naming** - `IFLOW_` + key name in settings.json (recommended)

action)\n```\n\n**Key Differentiators**:\n- BioMate has **structured audit logs** (iFlow has hook-based logging only)\n- BioMate tracks **workflow execution step-by-step** (iFlow tracks tool calls '~/.biomate/snapshots';\n\n  async createCheckpoint(workflowId: string): Promise<Checkpoint> {\n    return {\n      id: `checkpoint_${Date.now()}`,\n      workflowId,\n      timestamp: new Date(),\n      state: {\n        historyId: await this.getHistorySnapshot(),\n        datasetStates: await this.getDatasetStates(),\n        conversationContext: await this.getConversationContext()\n      }\n    };\n  }\n\n  async restore(checkpointId: string): Promise<void> {\n    const checkpoint = await this.loadCheckpoint(checkpointId);\n    await this.restoreHistoryState(checkpoint.state.historyId);\n      5→
     6→# Suspend and Resume
     7→
     8→> **Feature Overview**: iFlow CLI supports suspending (pausing) current tasks in interactive sessions and resuming them when needed.
     9→> 
    10→> **Learning Time**: 5 minutes
    11→> 
    12→> **Prerequisites**: Familiarity with basic command line operations such as `ctrl+z` and `fg`.
    13→
    14→## What is Suspend and Resume
    15→
    16→In iFlow CLI's interactive sessions, you may need to temporarily interrupt a currently running task to execute another higher-priority operation. The suspend and resume functionality allows you to use standard terminal commands to pause (suspend) the current iFlow session, then return (resume) to where you left off when you're ready.
    17→
    18→This feature leverages the Job Control capabilities of most modern shells (such as bash, zsh).
    19→
    20→## Core Operations
    21→
    22→| Operation | Command | Description |
    23→|-----------|---------|-------------|
    24→| Suspend | `ctrl+z` | Pauses the currently running iFlow process in the foreground and puts it in the background. |
    25→| Resume | `fg` or `fg %<job_number>` | Brings a background task back to the foreground to continue running. `fg` resumes the most recent task by default. Use `fg %1`, `fg %2`, etc. to resume specific tasks. |
    26→
    27→You can use the `jobs` command to view all background tasks and their numbers.
    28→
    29→## Workflow
    30→
    31→1. **Start interactive session**: Run `iflow` to enter interactive mode.
    32→2. **Execute task**: Interact with iFlow in the session, for example, run a script or ask a question.
    33→3. **Need to interrupt**: Suppose you need to check another file or run a quick command, but don't want to terminate the current iFlow session.
    34→4. **Suspend session**: Press `ctrl+z`. The iFlow CLI process will be paused, and you'll return to your shell prompt.
    35→5....
```

    10→# SDK
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→iFlow CLI SDK is an SDK for programmatic interaction with iFlow CLI. It allows developers to build AI-driven applications with conversation, tool execution, and task planning capabilities through the Agent Communication Protocol (ACP).
    15→
    16→**✨ Core Feature: SDK automatically manages iFlow processes - no manual configuration needed!**
    17→
    18→Currently provides **Python SDK**, with Java version coming soon!
    19→
    20→## System Requirements
    21→
    22→- **Python**: 3.8 or higher
    23→- **iFlow CLI**: 0.2.24 or higher
    24→- **Operating System**: Windows, macOS, Linux
    25→
    26→## Installation
    27→
    28→```bash
    29→pip install iflow-cli-sdk
    30→```
    31→
    32→## Quick Start
    33→
    34→### Basic Example
    35→
    36→The SDK automatically detects and starts iFlow processes without manual configuration:
    37→
    38→```python
    39→import asyncio
    40→from iflow_sdk import IFlowClient, AssistantMessage, TaskFinishMessage
    41→
    42→async def main():
    43→    # SDK automatically handles:
    44→    # 1. Detect if iFlow is installed
    45→    # 2. Start iFlow process (if not running)
    46→    # 3. Find available port and establish connection
    47→    # 4. Automatically clean up resources on exit
    48→    async with IFlowClient() as client:
    49→        await client.send_message("Hello, iFlow!")
    50→
    51→        async for message in client.receive_messages():
    52→            if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage):
    53→                print(message.chunk.text, end="\n", flush=True)
    54→            elif isinstance(message, TaskFinishMessage):
    55→                break
    ...
```

  "content": "# iFlow Agent Task Management Architecture - Lessons for BioMate\n\n**Date**: 2026-01-13\n**Purpose**: Deep analysis of how iFlow creates, executes, and manages agent tasks - architectural patterns to adopt\n\n---\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nThis document focuses on the **how** of iFlow's agent task management, not just feature comparison. This enables:\n- Security isolation (agents can't exceed their permissions)\n- Specialization (each agent optimized for its domain)\n- Composability (agents can delegate to sub-agents)\n\n### 1.3 BioMate Current Architecture vs iFlow\n\n| Aspect | BioMate Current | iFlow Pattern | Gap |\n|--------|-----------------|---------------|-----|\n| Task Analysis | Intent parsing in `ai_assistant.py` | Explicit agent matching | BioMate lacks agent specialization |\n| Tool Selection | Tool search (2,177 tools) \u2192 ranking | Agent defines allowed tools | BioMate tools are global, not scoped |\n| Permission | Galaxy API key controls all | Per-agent tool permissions | BioMate lacks fine-grained control |\n| Specialization | LTM preferences per user | Agent types per domain | BioMate learns per-user, not per-domain |\n\n---\n\n## Part 2: Agent Task Execution Architecture\n\n### 2.1 iFlow's Agent Communication Protocol (ACP)\n\niFlow defines a **standardized message protocol** for agent communication:\n\n```python\n# Message Types in ACP\nAssistantMessage    # AI text response chunks\nToolCallMessage     # Tool execution requests/status\nPlanMessage         # Structured task plans\nTaskFinishMessage   # Task completion signals\n```\n\nEach message includes **AgentInfo**:\n```python\nclass AgentInfo:\n    agent_id: str           # Full agent identifier\n    task_id: Optional[str]  # Task/instance ID\n    agent_index: Optional[int]  # Agent index in task\n    timestamp: Optional[int]    # Creation timestamp\n```\n\n**Key Insight**: Every message is tagged with **who sent it** (agent_id), **what task** (task_id), and **when** (timestamp). \u25bc                \u25bc\n                                    \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510     \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510\n                                    \u2502 Waiting  \u2502     \u2502 Completed  \u2502\n                                    \u2502 for User \u2502     \u2502 (END_TURN) \u2502\n                                    \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518     \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518\n                                          \u2502\n                                          \u25bc\n                                    \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510\n                                    \u2502 Terminated   \u2502\n                                    \u2502 (MAX_TOKENS) \u2502\n                                    \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518\n```\n\n**Stop Reasons**:\n- `END_TURN` - Task completed successfully\n- `MAX_TOKENS` - Token limit reached, task incomplete\n- User interruption (suspend/resume)\n\n### 2.3 Tool Call Status Flow\n\n```\n\u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510     \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510     \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510     \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510\n\u2502 Pending  \u2502 \u2500\u2500\u25b6 \u2502 Running  \u2502 \u2500\u2500\u25b6 \u2502 Completed \u2502 or  \u2502 Failed    \u2502\n\u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518     \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518     \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518     \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518\n                      \u2502\n                      \u25bc\n               \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510\n               \u2502 Requires     \u2502\n               \u2502 Permission   \u2502\n               \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518\n```\n\n**Key Insight**: Tool calls have explicit **permission gates** before execution. BioMate should add this for sensitive bioinformatics operations.\n\n---\n\n## Part 3: Agent Task Management (Orchestration)\n\n### 3.1 Hierarchical Agent Delegation\n\niFlow supports **sub-agent** spawning with controlled scope:\n\n```\nMain Agent (Full permissions)\n    \u2502\n    \u251c\u2500\u2500 SubAgent A (code-reviewer)\n    \u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 Tools: [Read, Grep]  \u2190 Reduced scope\n    \u2502\n    \u251c\u2500\u2500 SubAgent B (doc-writer)\n    \u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 Tools: [Read, Write]  \u2190 Different scope\n    \u2502\n    \u2514\u2500\u2500 SubAgent C (data-scientist)\n        \u2514\u2500\u2500 Tools: [Read, Bash]  \u2190 Analysis scope\n```\n\n**Permission Inheritance**:\n```yaml\nisInheritTools: true   # Inherit parent's tool permissions\nisInheritMcps: false   # Don't inherit parent's MCP access\nallowedTools: [\"Read\"] # Explicit whitelist\n```\n\n**Key Insight**: Sub-agents can be **more restricted** than parent, never more permissive. This is a security pattern BioMate should adopt.\n\n### 3.2 Plan/Todo Integration\n\niFlow's `PlanMessage` is similar to BioMate's `TodoWrite` but integrated into the agent protocol:\n\n```python\nclass PlanMessage:\n    entries: List[PlanEntry]\n\nclass PlanEntry:\n    content: str        # Task description\n    priority: str       # Priority level\n    status: str         # pending/completed/in_progress\n```\n\n**Key Insight**: Plans are **first-class messages** in the protocol, not a separate tool. This enables:\n- Agents to communicate plans to each other\n- External systems to track agent planning\n- Audit trail of agent decisions\n\n### 3.3 Workflow Composition Pattern\n\niFlow composes complex workflows from:\n\n```\nWorkflow = Agents + Commands + IFLOW.md + MCP Tools\n```\n\n**Directory Structure**:\n```\n.iflow/\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 agents/           # Domain specialist definitions\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 reviewer.md\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 developer.md\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 commands/         # Reusable command scripts\n\u2502   \u2514\u2500\u2500 deploy.md\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 IFLOW.md          # Context documentation\n\u2514\u2500\u2500 settings.json     # MCP configuration\n```\n\n**Key Insight**: Workflows are **packages** that can be shared, installed, and versioned. This is a marketplace-ready pattern.\n\n---\n\n## Part 4: Architectural Recommendations for BioMate\n\n### 4.1 Agent Communication Protocol for BioMate\n\n**Current BioMate**: Ad-hoc message passing, no standardized protocol\n\n**Proposed**: Implement Biomate Communication Protocol (BCP)\n\n```typescript\n// backend/lib/galaxy/ai/protocol/bcp.ts\n\ntype BCPMessageType =\n  | 'assistant'      // AI text response\n  | 'tool_call'      // Tool execution\n  | 'workflow_plan'  // Workflow planning\n  | 'task_finish'    // Task completion\n  | 'learning'       // LTM update event\n\ninterface BCPMessage {\n  type: BCPMessageType;\n  agentInfo: {\n    agentId: string;      // e.g., \"workflow-generator-1736755200000\"\n    taskId?: string;      // e.g., \"rna-seq-analysis-001\"\n    stepIndex?: number;   // e.g., 3 (for multi-step workflows)\n    timestamp: number;\n  };\n  payload: any;\n}\n\ninterface TaskFinishPayload {\n  stopReason: 'end_turn' | 'max_tokens' | 'user_interrupt' | 'error';\n  result?: any;\n  error?: string;\n}\n```\n\n**Benefits**:\n- Standardized message format for all agent communication\n- Full audit trail with agent attribution\n- Multi-agent coordination support\n\n### 4.2 Agent Specialization for Bioinformatics\n\n**Current BioMate**: Single hybrid intelligence pipeline\n\n**Proposed**: Domain-specialized agents with tool boundaries\n\n```typescript\n// backend/lib/galaxy/ai/agents/agent_registry.ts\n\ninterface BiomateAgent {\n  agentType: string;\n  domain: string;           // e.g., \"genomics\", \"proteomics\", \"imaging\"\n  systemPrompt: string;\n  allowedToolCategories: string[];  // e.g., [\"genomics/*\", \"database/*\"]\n  preferredTools: string[];         // Tools this agent excels at\n  model?: string;\n  inheritToolsFromParent: boolean;\n}\n\nconst BIOMATE_AGENTS: BiomateAgent[] = [\n  {\n    agentType: \"genomics-analyst\",\n    domain: \"genomics\",\n    systemPrompt: \"You are a genomics analysis expert...\",\n    allowedToolCategories: [\"genomics/*\", \"database/ensembl\", \"database/ucsc\"],\n    preferredTools: [\"annotate_celltype_scRNA\", \"gene_set_enrichment_analysis\"],\n    inheritToolsFromParent: true\n  },\n  {\n    agentType: \"proteomics-analyst\",\n    domain: \"proteomics\",\n    systemPrompt: \"You are a proteomics analysis expert...\",\n    allowedToolCategories: [\"pharmacology/*\", \"database/uniprot\", \"database/pdb\"],\n    preferredTools: [\"docking_autodock_vina\", \"predict_binding_affinity\"],\n    inheritToolsFromParent: true\n  },\n  {\n    agentType: \"imaging-analyst\",\n    domain: \"bioimaging\",\n    systemPrompt: \"You are a biological imaging expert...\",\n    allowedToolCategories: [\"bioimaging/*\", \"cell_biology/*\"],\n    preferredTools: [\"segment_with_nn_unet\", \"register_images\"],\n    inheritToolsFromParent: true\n  }\n];\n```\n\n**Selection Logic**:\n```typescript\n// backend/lib/galaxy/ai/agents/agent_selector.ts\n\nasync function selectAgent(userRequest: string): Promise<BiomateAgent> {\n  // 1. Analyze request domain\n  const domain = await analyzeDomain(userRequest);\n\n  // 2. Find matching agent\n  const agent = BIOMATE_AGENTS.find(a => a.domain === domain);\n\n  // 3. Fall back to general agent if no match\n  return agent || GENERAL_PURPOSE_AGENT;\n}\n```\n\n### 4.3 Tool Permission Scoping\n\n**Current BioMate**: All tools accessible to all operations\n\n**Proposed**: Tool scoping by agent and user role\n\n```typescript\n// backend/lib/galaxy/ai/permissions/tool_permissions.ts\n\ninterface ToolPermission {\n  toolId: string;\n  allowedAgents: string[];      // Which agents can use this\n  requiredUserRole?: string;    // Minimum user role required\n  requiresConfirmation: boolean; // Ask user before executing\n  auditLevel: 'basic' | 'detailed' | 'full';\n}\n\nconst TOOL_PERMISSIONS: ToolPermission[] = [\n  {\n    toolId: \"delete_dataset\",\n    allowedAgents: [\"admin-agent\"],\n    requiredUserRole: \"admin\",\n    requiresConfirmation: true,\n    auditLevel: \"full\"\n  },\n  {\n    toolId: \"run_diffdock_with_smiles\",\n    allowedAgents: [\"proteomics-analyst\", \"pharmacology-analyst\"],\n    requiresConfirmation: false,\n    auditLevel: \"detailed\"\n  }\n];\n\nasync function checkToolPermission(\n  toolId: string,\n  agentType: string,\n  userRole: string\n): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; reason?: string }> {\n  const permission = TOOL_PERMISSIONS.find(p => p.toolId === toolId);\n\n  if (!permission) return { allowed: true }; // Default allow\n\n  if (!permission.allowedAgents.includes(agentType)) {\n    return { allowed: false, reason: `Agent ${agentType} cannot use ${toolId}` };\n  }\n\n  if (permission.requiredUserRole && userRole !== permission.requiredUserRole) {\n    return { allowed: false, reason: `Role ${permission.requiredUserRole} required` };\n  }\n\n  return { allowed: true };\n}\n```\n\n### 4.4 Task Lifecycle Management\n\n**Current BioMate**: Basic workflow execution tracking\n\n**Proposed**: Full task lifecycle with state management\n\n```typescript\n// backend/lib/galaxy/ai/tasks/task_manager.ts\n\ntype TaskState =\n  | 'created'\n  | 'agent_selected'\n

## 🤖 Message 2786 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2026-01-13T20:55:29.069Z*

I've completed the deep analysis of iFlow's agent task management architecture. Here's a summary of the key architectural learnings:

## Summary: What BioMate Should Learn from iFlow's Agent Task Architecture

### Core Architectural Patterns to Adopt

**1. Agent Communication Protocol (ACP → BCP)**
- Standardized message types: `assistant`, `tool_call`, `workflow_plan`, `task_finish`, `learning`
- Every message tagged with `AgentInfo { agentId, taskId, stepIndex, timestamp }`
- All messages routed through AuditService (backend integration, not user-facing)

**2. Domain Agent Specialization**
- iFlow separates "which agent" from "which tools"
- Each agent has `allowedTools` whitelist (security isolation)
- Permission inheritance: `isInheritTools: true/false`
- BioMate implementation: `genomics-analyst`, `proteomics-analyst`, `imaging-analyst` with scoped tool access

**3. Task Lifecycle State Machine**
```
Created → Agent Selected → Planning → Executing → Completed
                              ↓           ↓
                         Waiting User   Checkpoint (for rollback)
```

**4. Workflow Composition**
- iFlow packages: Agents + Commands + IFLOW.md + settings.json
- BioMate equivalent: Agent registry + Tool permissions + BIOMATE.md + LTM

### Key Differentiator (BioMate Advantage)
- iFlow: Manual agent curation only
- BioMate: **Automatic learning** from corrections → preferences → procedures
- Strategy: Combine iFlow's **structured agents** with BioMate's **automatic personalization**

### Documents Created

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `docs/05-data/20260113_IFLOW_AGENT_TASK_ARCHITECTURE.md` | Deep architectural analysis with implementation code |
| `docs/architecture/29_agent_task_orchestration.drawio.xml` | Visual diagram of agent task orchestration |

### Updated Files
- `20260112_SYSTEM_AUDIT_AND_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md` - Added Phase 6 architectural patterns

The hooks are wrapped at the backend level (users don't configure them) - they're part of the BCP message routing system that feeds into AuditService automatically.

Checkpointing / State Persistence\n\n**iFlow**: Can suspend and resume agent tasks with full state preservation.\n\n**BioMate Gap**: No checkpoint mechanism. If orchestration fails mid-way, must restart.\n\n**Proposed Enhancement**:\n```python\nclass CheckpointManager:\n    def save_checkpoint(self, session_id: str, state: OrchestrationState):\n        \"\"\"Save orchestration state to Redis/SQLite\"\"\"\n\n    def restore_checkpoint(self, session_id: str) -> Optional[OrchestrationState]:\n        \"\"\"Restore from last checkpoint\"\"\"\n```\n\n#### 3. Sub-Agent Spawning with Permission Inheritance\n\n**iFlow**: Parent agents can spawn sub-agents that inherit tool permissions.\n\n**BioMate Gap**: Specialists are pre-defined, not dynamically spawned.\n\n**Proposed Enhancement** (if needed):\n```python\nclass DynamicSpecialist:\n    def spawn_sub_specialist(self, task: str, parent_tools: List[str]) -> Specialist:\n        \"\"\"Spawn a focused sub-agent for a specific sub-task\"\"\"\n```\n\n#### 4. Structured Planning Stage\n\n**iFlow**: Explicit plan generation and approval before execution.\n\n**BioMate Gap**: Domain routing happens implicitly. User doesn't see the routing decision.\n\n**Proposed Enhancement**:\n```python\nclass PlanningStage:\n    def generate_plan(self, query: str) -> WorkflowPlan:\n        \"\"\"Generate explicit plan for user approval\"\"\"\n        return WorkflowPlan(\n            domains=[\"transcriptomics\", \"genomics\"],\n            specialists_to_consult=[\"rna_seq_expert\", \"variant_caller_expert\"],\n            estimated_tools=[\"salmon\", \"star\", \"gatk\"],\n            rationale=\"Query involves both expression and variant analysis...\"\n        )\n```\n\n#### 5. Tool Permission Scoping\n\n**iFlow**: Strict tool permissions per agent type.\n\n**BioMate Gap**: Specialists get filtered tools by domain, but no strict permission enforcement.\n\n**Proposed Enhancement**:\n```python\nDOMAIN_TOOL_PERMISSIONS = {\n    \"genomics\": {\"bwa\", \"gatk\", \"deepvariant\", \"samtools\"},\n    \"transcriptomics\": {\"star\", \"salmon\", \"deseq2\", \"kallisto\"},\n    \"structural_biology\": {\"alphafold\", \"autodock\", \"pymol\"},\n    # ... strict boundaries\n}\n\ndef enforce_permissions(specialist: str, requested_tools: List[str]) -> List[str]:\n    \"\"\"Only allow tools within permission scope\"\"\"\n    allowed = DOMAIN_TOOL_PERMISSIONS.get(specialist, set())\n    return [t for t in requested_tools if t in allowed]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Enhancements\n\nBased on the gap analysis, prioritized enhancements:\n\n### Priority 1: Standardized Message Protocol (BCP)\n\n**Rationale**: Enables better debugging, distributed tracing, and audit logging.\n\n**Implementation Effort**: Low\n**Impact**: Medium (debugging, observability)\n\n### Priority 2: Checkpoint/Resume Capability\n\n**Rationale**: Long-running workflows should survive failures.\n\n**Implementation Effort**: Medium\n**Impact**: High (reliability)\n\n### Priority 3: Explicit Planning Stage\n\n**Rationale**: User transparency and approval before expensive LLM calls.\n\n**Implementation Effort**: Medium\n**Impact**: High (user trust, cost control)\n\n### Priority 4: Tool Permission Enforcement\n\n**Rationale**: Prevents cross-domain tool hallucination.\n\n**Implementation Effort**: Low\n**Impact**: Medium (accuracy)\n\n### Not Recommended\n\n- **Dynamic Sub-Agent Spawning**: BioMate's pre-defined domain specialists are sufficient for bioinformatics use cases. ## 🤖 Message 2842 (assistant)

I have completed the agent hierarchy analysis. Here's a summary of what was created:

## Documentation Created

1. **`docs/05-data/20260113_BIOMATE_AGENT_HIERARCHY.md`** - Comprehensive documentation of BioMate's existing 3-layer agent architecture:
   - Layer 1: Intent Classification (UnifiedIntentRouter - 10 intent types)
   - Layer 2: Agent Orchestration (EnhancedDomainRouter → DomainSpecialistPool → WorkflowAssembler)
   - Layer 3: Supporting Components (UserPatternsAdapter, BenchmarkKnowledgeDB, AuditService)

2. **`docs/architecture/30_biomate_agent_hierarchy.drawio.xml`** - Visual diagram showing the complete agent flow from user query to Galaxy workflow output

3. **`docs/architecture/31_biomate_vs_iflow_comparison.drawio.xml`** - Side-by-side comparison diagram with gap analysis

4. **Updated `20260112_SYSTEM_AUDIT_AND_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md`** - Added Phase 8 documenting agent hierarchy findings

## Key Findings

**BioMate already has ~80% of iFlow's agent capabilities:**

| Already Implemented | Genuine Gaps |
|---------------------|--------------|
| Intent classification (10 types) | Standardized message protocol |
| Domain routing (15 bio domains) | Checkpointing/resume |
| Parallel execution (ThreadPoolExecutor) | Explicit planning stage |
| User learning (SQLite) | Strict tool permissions |
| LRU caching for LLM decisions | |
| Hybrid keyword + LLM routing | |

**What we can ACTUALLY leverage from iFlow:**

| Gap | Effort | Impact | Priority |
|-----|--------|--------|----------|
| Message Protocol (BCP) | Low | Medium | P1 |
| Checkpoint/Resume | Medium | High | P2 |
| Explicit Planning Stage | Medium | High | P3 |
| Tool Permission Enforcement | Low | Medium | P4 |

These 4 enhancements would improve reliability, observability, and user trust without requiring fundamental architecture changes.

Now I have a clear picture. Let me answer your questions directly:

## 1. Galaxy's Checkpoint/Resume Capabilities

**Galaxy does NOT have true checkpoint/resume.** What Galaxy has:

| Galaxy Feature | What It Does | NOT Same As Checkpoint |
|----------------|--------------|------------------------|
| `InvocationState` | Track workflow states: NEW → READY → SCHEDULED → FAILED/CANCELLED | No state persistence for recovery |
| Job `RESUBMITTED` state | Mark jobs that were re-run | Manual re-run, not automatic resume |
| Step-level tracking | Each step has NEW/READY/SCHEDULED state | Tracks progress, doesn't save it |
| `cancel_invocation()` | Stop a running workflow | No "resume cancelled workflow" |

**Galaxy's limitation**: If a workflow fails at step 15 of 20, you must restart from step 1 (unless you manually create a new workflow starting from step 15).

**What iFlow has that Galaxy doesn't**: Full state serialization to Redis/SQLite so you can suspend mid-execution and resume later with all context preserved.

## 2. Relation to Test Harness - Should It Have Checkpointing?

Looking at our `benchmark_suite.py`:

```python
class BenchmarkStatus(str, Enum):
    PENDING = "pending"
    RUNNING = "running"
    COMPLETE = "complete"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"
```

**Current limitation**: If running 100 benchmark runs and it fails at run 50, you lose all progress.

**Yes, the test harness SHOULD have checkpointing:**

```python
# What we should add to benchmark_suite.py:

def save_checkpoint(self, results: BenchmarkResults, checkpoint_dir: str):
    """Save checkpoint after each successful run."""
    checkpoint_path = Path(checkpoint_dir) / f"{results.scenario_name}_checkpoint.json"
    with open(checkpoint_path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(results.to_dict(), f)

def resume_from_checkpoint(self, scenario_name: str, checkpoint_dir: str) -> BenchmarkResults:
    """Resume from last checkpoint."""
    checkpoint_path = Path(checkpoint_dir) / f"{scenario_name}_checkpoint.json"
    if checkpoint_path.exists():
        with open(checkpoint_path) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        # Return partially completed results
        # Skip already-completed runs
```

**Benefits for benchmarking**:
- Long benchmark suites (hours/days) can survive interruptions
- Can pause overnight and resume
- Failure in one run doesn't lose completed runs

## 3. What Do I Mean by Tool Permissions?

Looking at `domain_specialist.py`:

```python
def consult_specialists(
    self,
    query: str,
    domains: List[str],
    tools_per_domain: int = 15  # <-- SOFT FILTER
):
```

**Current behavior (Soft Filtering)**:
- Genomics specialist ASKS for genomics-related tools
- Gets back 15 filtered tools
- But nothing PREVENTS the LLM from recommending any tool it knows about

**iFlow's approach (Strict Enforcement)**:
```yaml
agentType: "genomics-analyst"
allowedTools: ["bwa", "gatk", "deepvariant", "samtools"]  # WHITELIST
```

The agent physically CANNOT invoke tools outside its whitelist.

**Why it matters for BioMate**:
- LLM might hallucinate tool names
- Cross-domain recommendations could be inappropriate (proteomics tool for genomics data)
- Strict permissions = guaranteed tool validity

**Proposed fix**:
```python
DOMAIN_TOOL_PERMISSIONS = {
    "genomics": {"bwa", "gatk", "deepvariant", "samtools", "bcftools"},
    "transcriptomics": {"star", "salmon", "deseq2", "kallisto", "htseq"},
    "proteomics": {"maxquant", "dia-nn", "msfragger", "percolator"},
    # ...
}

def validate_recommendation(self, domain: str, tool_id: str) -> bool:
    """Enforce that recommended tools are within domain scope."""
    allowed = DOMAIN_TOOL_PERMISSIONS.get(domain, set())
    return tool_id.lower() in allowed
```

## Summary

| Topic | Status | Recommendation |
|-------|--------|----------------|
| Galaxy checkpoint/resume | **Galaxy has tracking, not checkpoint** | We need to add our own state persistence if we want true resume |
| Test harness checkpointing | **Not implemented** | Yes, add it - benchmarks can take hours |
| Tool permissions | **Soft filtering only** | Consider adding validation layer |

Shall I implement checkpointing for the test harness or create the tool permission enforcement?

```
# Nextflow Caching and Resume: Key Features

## How It Works

Nextflow automatically saves all task executions to a task cache, enabling recovery from errors and iterative pipeline development. The `-resume` flag activates this capability: `nextflow run <pipeline> -resume`

The mechanism relies on two components:
1. **Task cache** (.nextflow/cache directory) – stores task metadata using LevelDB
2. **Work directory** – preserves task output files and execution artifacts

## What Gets Cached

Each task receives a unique hash computed from:
- Session ID and task name
- Container image, environment modules, and Conda/Spack environments
- Task inputs, scripts, and global variables referenced in scripts
- The `ext` directive properties and bundled scripts
- Whether it's a stub run

The system stores serialized task metadata (the "task entry") alongside input variables for resumption purposes.

## Usage

Enable resumption with `-resume` in your command or configuration. To resume from a specific earlier run, specify its session ID:

```
nextflow run rnaseq-nf -resume 4dc656d2-c410-44c8-bc32-7dd0ea87bebf
```

Use the `log` command to view previous runs and task execution history.

## Key Limitations

- **Both caches must persist**: Deleting `.nextflow/cache` or work directories prevents successful resumption
- **File modifications invalidate cache**: Changing inputs, process names, scripts, or container images triggers re-execution
- **Race conditions disrupt caching**: Global variables declared in closures can cause non-deterministic inputs
- **NFS inconsistencies**: Shared filesystems may report inconsistent timestamps; use "lenient" caching mode to mitigate

## Troubleshooting Tools

Use `-dump-hashes` to compare task hashes between runs and identify what changed, revealing why tasks re-executed unexpectedly.
```

## 🤖 Message 2938 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2026-01-13T21:15:54.639Z*

**Excellent news!** Nextflow has **built-in checkpoint/resume** that's one of its core features.

## Nextflow's Resume Capabilities

| Feature | How It Works |
|---------|--------------|
| **`-resume` flag** | `nextflow run pipeline.nf -resume` skips completed tasks |
| **Automatic caching** | Every task cached in `.nextflow/cache` (LevelDB) |
| **Hash-based validation** | Re-runs only if inputs/scripts/containers change |
| **Work directory** | Outputs preserved in `work/` for resumption |
| **Cloud support** | Works with S3, GCS, Azure blob storage |

**Example**:
```bash
# First run - fails at step 15
nextflow run rnaseq.nf

# Resume - skips steps 1-14, continues from 15
nextflow run rnaseq.nf -resume

# Resume specific session
nextflow run rnaseq.nf -resume 4dc656d2-c410-44c8-bc32-7dd0ea87bebf
```

## What This Means for BioMate

| Component | Needs Custom Checkpoint? | Why |
|-----------|-------------------------|-----|
| **Workflow Execution** | **NO** - Nextflow handles it | Built-in `-resume` |
| **Agent Orchestration** | **YES** - still needed | Conversation context, routing decisions not in Nextflow |
| **Test Harness** | **YES** - still needed | Benchmarks don't use Nextflow's mechanism |

Let me update the plan to reflect this.

## 🤖 Message 2952 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2026-01-13T21:16:47.139Z*

Done. Both documents are now updated with Nextflow's checkpoint/resume capabilities.

## Summary: Checkpoint Comparison

| System | Checkpoint/Resume | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| **Galaxy** | NO - tracking only | Must restart from step 1 on failure |
| **Nextflow** | **YES - built-in** | `-resume` flag, automatic caching |
| **iFlow** | YES - state serialization | Redis/SQLite persistence |

## What BioMate Still Needs (Even with Nextflow)

| Component | Nextflow Helps? | Custom Checkpoint Needed? |
|-----------|-----------------|---------------------------|
| **Workflow Execution** | YES | NO - Nextflow handles it |
| **Agent Orchestration** | NO | YES - conversation context, routing decisions |
| **Test Harness** | NO | YES - benchmark progress |

## Key Nextflow Features

```bash
# Resume from failure
nextflow run pipeline.nf -resume

# Resume specific session
nextflow run pipeline.nf -resume 4dc656d2-c410-44c8

# Debug why tasks re-ran
nextflow run pipeline.nf -resume -dump-hashes
```

**Nextflow caches based on**:
- Input files (path + timestamp + size)
- Scripts and process definitions
- Container images
- Environment modules

**BioMate's Nextflow readiness**:
- `backend/nf-core-modules/` - module library
- `backend/biomni_workflows/nextflow/` - 100+ workflows
- `workflow_converters/nextflow_converter.py` - converter

Sources:
- [Nextflow Caching and Resuming Documentation](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/cache-and-resume.html)
- [Demystifying Nextflow Resume - Seqera](https://seqera.io/blog/demystifying-nextflow-resume/)
- [Workflow Caching and Checkpointing Tutorial](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/workflows-nextflow/10-workflow_checkpoint_caching.html)

  1405→        is_valid, message = self.validate_tool_recommendation(domain, tool.tool_id)
  1406→        if is_valid:
  1407→            validated_tools.append(tool)
  1408→        else:
  1409→            log.warning(f"Rejected tool recommendation: {message}")
  1410→
  1411→    recommendation.recommended_tools = validated_tools
  1412→    return recommendation
  1413→```

Memory-based session context |\n| `record_interaction()` | Log for episodic learning |\n\n**Tool ID Normalization:**\n```python\n# AI database format:  biomni/database/query_uniprot\n# Galaxy format:       biomni_database_query_uniprot\ndef _normalize_tool_id(tool_id):\n    if tool_id.startswith('biomni/'):\n        return tool_id.replace('/', '_')\n    return tool_id\n```\n\n#### 6.2.2 llm_client.py - Multi-Provider LLM Client (563 lines)\n\n| Provider | Model(s) | API Key Required | Notes |\n|----------|----------|------------------|-------|\n| `anthropic` | claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-opus-4-5 | Yes | Primary |\n| `openai` | gpt-4o, gpt-4-turbo | Yes | - |\n| `gemini` | gemini-2.0-flash-exp | Yes | Google |\n| `deepseek` | deepseek-chat, deepseek-coder | Yes | OpenAI-compatible |\n| `ollama` | qwen3:32b, llama3.3:70b | No | Local |\n| `zhipu` | glm-4.7, glm-4.6v-flash | Yes | Chinese |\n| `local` | Any | Optional | LM Studio, vLLM |\n\n**Automatic Fallback:**\n```python\n# If primary provider fails, automatically try Claude\nasync def generate_async(self, prompt, **kwargs):\n    try:\n        # Try primary provider\n        return await self._generate_{provider}(prompt, **kwargs)\n    except Exception:\n        # Fallback to Claude 3.5 Sonnet\n        if self.provider != 'anthropic':\n            self.provider = 'anthropic'\n            self.model = 'claude-sonnet-4-5'\n            return await self._generate_anthropic(prompt, **kwargs)\n```\n\n#### 6.2.3 enhanced_workflow_generator.py - Template + RAG (552 lines)\n\n| Strategy | When Used | Confidence |\n|----------|-----------|------------|\n| `template_based` | Template score \u2265 15 | 0.95 |\n| `hybrid` | Template score 8-15 | 0.85 |\n| `rag_assisted` | Template score < 8 | 0.70 |\n\n**Generation Flow:**\n1. Search templates \u2192 Get relevance score\n2. Select strategy based on score\n3. Generate workflow using selected strategy\n4. Auto-install missing tools (if enabled)\n5. Add metadata and timestamps\n\n#### 6.2.4 galaxy_workflow_generator.py - Tool-Constrained (993 lines)\n\n**Critical Design Principle:** LLM can ONLY use tools from the retrieved tool index.\n\n**Generation Flow:**\n1. `_retrieve_tools_from_index()` \u2192 UnifiedToolSearch (LLM + vector + FTS5)\n2. `_generate_workflow_structure()` \u2192 LLM designs workflow with retrieved tools ONLY\n3. `select_datasets_for_workflow()` \u2192 WorkflowDatasetSelector assigns datasets\n4. `_build_galaxy_workflow_json()` \u2192 Build .ga format with LLM parameter generation\n5. Collect citations from ToolKnowledgeProvider\n\n**LLM Parameter Generation:**\n- For data source tools (query, fetch, download)\n- Uses `LLMParameterGenerator` to infer parameters from user intent\n- Returns confidence scores for each parameter\n\n### 6.3 Workflow Generation Strategies\n\n| Strategy | Source | Confidence | When Used |\n|----------|--------|------------|-----------|\n| `template_reuse` | WorkflowSearchRAG | 0.8+ | Exact template match |\n| `template_adapt` | EnhancedWorkflowGenerator | 0.5-0.8 | Adapt existing template |\n| `tool_constrained` | GalaxyWorkflowGenerator | <0.5 | Generate from scratch |\n| `multi_agent` | AgentOrchestrator | Variable | Complex multi-domain |\n\n### 6.4 Key Findings\n\n#### 6.4.1 Strengths\n- **Lazy loading**: Components only loaded when needed (reduces memory)\n- **Multi-provider LLM**: Supports 7 providers with automatic fallback\n- **Tool validation**: Prevents hallucinated tools in workflows\n- **Citation integration**: Automatic DOI/PMID injection\n- **Progress tracking**: Real-time progress callbacks for UI\n\n#### 6.4.2 Issues Found\n\n| Priority | Issue | Location | Impact |\n|----------|-------|--

## 🤖 Message 3494 (assistant)

*Timestamp: 2026-01-14T20:16:32.322Z*

The current `useWorkflowExecution` hook in `frontend/client/src/hooks/useWorkflowExecution.ts` can only track **one workflow at a time**:

```typescript
// Current implementation - SINGLE workflow tracking
const [state, setState] = useState<WorkflowExecutionState>({
  workflowId: null,       // Only ONE workflow ID
  invocationId: null,     // Only ONE invocation ID
  workflowState: null,
  steps: new Map(),       // Steps for ONE workflow
  ...
});
```

**The Problem**: If a user starts Workflow A, then starts Workflow B while A is still running, the hook loses track of Workflow A because it overwrites the state with B's data.

**A `useMultiWorkflowExecution` hook would track multiple workflows simultaneously**:

```typescript
// Proposed - MULTI workflow tracking
const [executions, setExecutions] = useState<Map<string, WorkflowExecutionState>>(new Map());

// Each invocation tracked independently
executions.get('invocation_A')  // Still running
executions.get('invocation_B')  // Also running
executions.get('invocation_C')  // Completed
```

**Current Workaround**: Users can see multiple running workflows in the `WorkflowHistoryPanel` (the "My Workflows" sidebar), which fetches from `/api/invocations`. But the real-time SSE updates only work for one workflow in the chat view.

Do you want me to implement this multi-workflow hook, or is the current single-workflow tracking sufficient for your use case?
